articles.title: Added Value of CT Bone Reading Software in the Detection of Subtle Bone Metastases From Breast Cancer: Comparison with Standard Thorax CT.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study is to evaluate the additional diagnostic value of CT Bone Reading software in detecting rib metastases on thoracic computed tomography in patients with breast cancer and to examine its effectiveness on lesion detection, evaluation time, and inter-reader agreement. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 110 patients with breast cancer and bone metastases who underwent both thoracic computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography-CT scans between January 2022 and January 2026. For lesion-level assessment, suspected rib lesions were also evaluated using available longitudinal follow-up imaging. Two radiologists independently evaluated conventional CT and CT Bone Reading images in separate reading sessions at least 2 weeks apart. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Cohen's κ statistic. RESULTS: In lesion-based analysis with conventional CT, Reader 1 detected 510 lesions (81.6%) and Reader 2 detected 577 lesions (92.3%), while CT Bone Reading allowed for the detection of an additional 115 (22.5%) and 48 (8.3%) lesions for Readers 1 and 2, respectively. The additionally detected lesions demonstrated a non-uniform distribution, with a marked predominance in the mid-rib region (levels 5th-8th). CT Bone Reading-assisted evaluation enabled the detection of significantly smaller lesions compared to routine CT for both readers (Reader 1: 8.0 mm vs 5.0 mm; Reader 2: 7.0 mm vs 5.0 mm; P < 0.001 for both). Evaluation time was significantly decreased from 129.22 ± 27.22 s to 64.94 ± 17.16 s for Reader 1 and from 122.99 ± 26.04 s to 64.44 ± 18.71 s for Reader 2 (P < 0.001 for both). Inter-reader agreement was excellent for measurements obtained by CT Bone Reading-derived evaluation (ICC ≥0.965; κ ≥0.947). CONCLUSION: CT Bone Reading software increases the detection rates of rib lesions, reduces interpretation times, and demonstrates excellent inter-reader reproducibility compared to conventional CT assessment, with less experienced readers achieving the highest incremental throughput. By providing a comprehensive and continuous view of the ribs, this technique has the potential to improve diagnostic performance without additional radiation exposure, particularly in anatomically complex regions such as the mid ribs. Ultimately, this approach can enhance workflow efficiency during routine clinical practices.

articles.title: Radhawk: An AI-driven Recommender for Pediatric Radiology Education.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The unprecedented growth of technology and unfiltered information has led to cognitive overload and educational gaps in radiology. Radiologists and trainees often require "just-in-time" educational content while interpreting unfamiliar or infrequently encountered examinations, yet identifying reliable and appropriately targeted resources within the time constraints of the reading room can be challenging. This need is particularly relevant in pediatric radiology, where normal imaging appearances vary with age and development. Radhawk was developed as a scalable, artificial intelligence-driven intelligent tutoring system that delivers personalized, real-time educational resources to learners and radiologists, creating a precision curriculum tailored to each user's needs and clinical context. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Radhawk integrates with existing picture archiving and communication systems and a custom learning management system (RADiology's Intelligent Adaptive Learning). It utilizes natural language processing and machine learning algorithms to analyze imaging study information and provides results based on user preferences. The system's scalable architecture is built on Amazon Web Services, ensuring adaptability across multiple hospital systems. RESULTS: Radhawk successfully provides tailored recommendations for educational materials, including interactive courses, anatomical references, and case studies. Key features include: (1) Generation of personalized curricula based on learner performance and needs, (2) Presentation of age and gender-matched "normal" images for comparison, (3) Creation of user-specific heat maps to identify strengths and areas for improvement, and (4) Incorporation of expert subspecialist preferences to inform user choices. CONCLUSION: Radhawk replaces generic web searches with a knowledge-focused approach, providing instant access to high-quality, relevant resources. This precision education solution has the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy, enhance learning experiences, and address the shortage of specialized pediatric radiologists. Future plans include external testing across multiple pediatric radiology departments to validate Radhawk's scalability, acceptance, and value in real-world settings.

articles.title: Short-Duration [18F]florbetapir PET Reconstructions: Centiloid Agreement and Temporal-Window Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Shorter [18F]florbetapir PET acquisitions could improve workflow, but the effects of reconstruction duration and temporal-window position on Centiloid values are not well characterized. We evaluated quantitative agreement across short-duration reconstructions, temporal-window effects, and visual agreement. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included a primary cohort of 32 patients with early 1-, 2-, and 5-min reconstructions and a 10-min reference. A temporal-window cohort of 22 patients underwent early and late 5-min analysis. A validation cohort of 37 examinations underwent early, centered, and late 1- and 5-min reconstructions and a 10-min reference. Two readers independently classified early 1-min, early 5-min, and 10-min images across three separate reading sessions. Centiloid agreement was assessed using paired differences, Bland-Altman limits of agreement, and categorical agreement. RESULTS: In the primary cohort, mean differences from the 10-min reference were -3.70, -2.97, and -1.65 CL for early 1-, 2-, and 5-min reconstructions, respectively. In the temporal-window cohort, late 5-min values averaged 2.86 CL higher than early values. The validation cohort reproduced both findings: early-to-late shifts were +5.53 CL at 1 min and +3.07 CL at 5 min. In the reader study, agreement with 10 min was 70.3%-86.5% at 1 min and 94.6%-100% at 5 min; interreader κ was 0.49, 0.77, and 0.89 at 1, 5, and 10 min, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Early short-duration reconstructions yielded systematically lower Centiloid values, while later temporal windows yielded higher values at fixed duration. Visual agreement with 10 min was high at 5 min but lower at 1 min. Reconstruction duration and frame timing should be standardized before abbreviated protocols are considered substitutes for standard 10-min imaging.

articles.title: Moyamoya-Type Collaterals in ACTA2 p. Arg179 Related Arteriopathy: Challenging the Paradigm of Absent Neovascularization-A Longitudinal DSA Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: ACTA2 p. Arg179 variants can cause a distinctive cerebrovascular arteriopathy historically described lacking classic moyamoya basal collaterals. Limited data on collateral architecture and surgical outcomes have led to uncertainty regarding revascularization strategies. The purpose of this study is to provide a systematic longitudinal DSA assessment of collateral patterns and postoperative findings in pediatric ACTA2-associated cerebrovascular disease. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Ten pediatric patients with genetically confirmed ACTA2 mutations underwent DSA imaging. Eight consecutive patients with neurological instability and confirmed hemodynamic compromise underwent surgical revascularization (indirect or combined direct-indirect). Two patients with stable neurological status were managed conservatively. Paired DSA (7 patients) and magnetic resonance angiography (5 patients) were performed at baseline and follow-up of the operated cohort. Collaterals were classified as classic moyamoya-type, distal moyamoya-type, leptomeningeal, or duropial. Postoperative revascularization was graded using Matsushima classification. RESULTS: Mean baseline vessel calibers demonstrated marked proximal ectasia (petrous ICA 8.4 ± 2.8 mm vs. normative 3.8 ± 0.4) transitioning to distal stenosis (supraclinoid ICA 2.6 ± 0.7 mm vs. normative 3.3 ± 0.3). Classic moyamoya-type collaterals were present in 2 patients at baseline and in 5 patients at follow-up. Postoperative Matsushima grading demonstrated Grade A/B in 6 patients, with surgical collateralization remaining patent and sufficient up to 14 years. CONCLUSIONS: ACTA2 p. Arg179 related cerebral arteriopathy demonstrates moyamoya-type collaterals challenging the historical paradigm of absent collateralization. Robust surgical neovascularization comparable to idiopathic moyamoya may support revascularization in symptomatic pediatric patients with confirmed hemodynamic compromise.

articles.title: 2024-2025 Academic Neuroradiology Workforce and Practice Survey: Faculty FTE and Effort, Recruitment and Retirement Benchmarks.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Rising RVU targets and clinical workloads in academic neuroradiology raise concerns about diagnostic accuracy, patient safety, faculty burnout, and erosion of education/research missions. This national survey of division chiefs characterized current practice patterns, effort models, moonlighting, operational factors, compensation, protected time, grant support, and perceptions of sustainable productivity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Web-based survey of academic neuroradiology division chiefs (American Society of Neuroradiology directory), with up to three reminders. 51 responses were collected anonymously and analyzed descriptively in Microsoft Excel. Questions covered workforce, clinical effort models, workload exceedance drivers, moonlighting, leadership protected time, and grant support. RESULTS: Divisions had median 11 FTE (25th-75th: 7-17.25); faculty were mostly full-time (median 90% at 1.0 FTE). Retirement risk was low short-term (median 0% in 2 years, 10% in 5 years); median 2 hires/year. Median clinical effort was 74% cFTE. Effort models split between shift-based (47%) and RVU-target (45%; typically, 40th-70th percentile AAARAD); volume caps used in only 8%. Targets were frequently exceeded, mainly due to moonlighting/financial incentives (49%) and voluntary work (32%). Moonlighting was offered in 52% of divisions (median 50% participation), yielding typical additional income of $26K-$100K/year. Protected effort medians: 20% (division chiefs), 10% (fellowship directors). Grant support was commensurate with funding in most divisions; 62% received "cap gap" support for federal grants. CONCLUSION: Academic neuroradiology faces intense clinical demands, and relies heavily on voluntary and incentivized faculty moonlighting. These findings highlight the need for accurate productivity benchmarks, operational improvements, and stronger institutional protections to sustain quality, safety, faculty satisfaction, and the academic mission.
authors: ASNR Neuroradiology Division Chief Working Group

articles.title: Advanced Practice Providers in Spinal CSF Leak Programs: A Multi-Institutional Study of Current Roles and Perceived Impact on Patient Care.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Advanced practice providers (APPs), including nurse practitioners and physician assistants, are increasingly integrated into radiology practices. However, their utilization and clinical responsibilities in dedicated spinal CSF leak programs have not been characterized. Using a multicenter survey, we investigated APP training, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges of APP integration at US spinal CSF leak programs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A survey was distributed to physicians at US institutions with dedicated spinal CSF leak programs and APP involvement. Candidate institutions were identified through the International Society for Spinal CSF Leak and American Society of Spine Radiology. Survey questions addressed program characteristics, APP training and structure, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges. Responses were summarized descriptively. RESULTS: Twelve institutions completed the survey. Eight (67%) reported caring for more than 250 spinal CSF leak patients annually. APPs included nurse practitioners at 4 centers (33%), physician assistants at 3 (25%), and both at 5 (42%); 7 centers (58%) had APPs dedicated exclusively to spinal CSF leak care. APP training was primarily informal and on-the-job at all institutions. Common primary APP responsibilities included obtaining outside imaging, patient intake and symptom review, procedure and sedation orders, informed consent, post-procedural follow-up, pain management, and treatment of rebound intracranial hypertension. Shared APP and physician responsibilities commonly included outside record review, determining evaluation urgency, preliminary imaging review, sedation assessment, and multidisciplinary coordination. Procedural responsibilities such as lumbar puncture, intrathecal contrast administration, myelography planning, and CSF leak treatment were primarily performed by physicians in most programs. At least 75% of respondents strongly agreed that APP participation improved continuity of care, patient communication/accessibility, clinic efficiency, patient satisfaction, physician administrative burden, and multidisciplinary coordination. Common barriers included funding/support, billing/reimbursement, and limited procedural privileges. CONCLUSIONS: APPs are widely integrated into dedicated spinal CSF leak programs, with substantial involvement in pre-procedural evaluation, care coordination, and post-procedural management, while advanced myelography and CSF leak treatment remain predominantly physician-directed. APP participation was perceived to improve patient care and clinical workflow. These findings provide a framework for APP integration into specialized spinal CSF leak programs.

articles.title: Automated Detection of Endoleaks in CT Angiography Using a Single Deep Learning Model.
articles.abstract: AIM: Detecting endoleaks on post-EVAR CT scans, especially in the presence of artifacts caused by embolic agents like Onyx, is a challenging but critical task. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based method for endoleak detection using a single object detection model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective dataset comprising 249 CT scans was used, divided into training (129 scans) and test (120 scans) datasets. Ground truth annotations were obtained through 3D manual segmentation, and a preprocessing pipeline was applied. The model was trained on slices extracted from the training dataset and validated using standard metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, and AUC. RESULTS: The model achieved high performance at both the per-slice and per-series levels. Per-slice detection yielded a ROC AUC of 96%, with a sensitivity of 91%, specificity of 93%, PPV of 55%, and NPV of 99%. At the per-series level, sensitivity and specificity were 93% and 95%, respectively. Notably, our method introduces a per-slice detection metric, which was not reported in previous studies, and uses a single model, making it computationally efficient and easy to train. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning for endoleak detection, offering a robust and efficient tool for clinical practice. Future work could focus on expanding the dataset and integrating additional predictive capabilities, such as endoleak classification and localization.

articles.title: Percutaneous Deep Venous Arterialization Using the Boomerang® Catheter System.
Ex Vivo Histopathological Validation of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging for Diagnosing Intimal and Medial Calcification in a Single Femoropopliteal Lesion.
articles.abstract: Optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) is available to guide atherectomy for severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions in patients with lower extremity artery disease, although its diagnostic accuracy has not been histologically validated. We evaluated the diagnostic capability of OFDI through histopathological co-registration. A total of 38 OFDI cross-sectional images from a single vessel in one patient were successfully co-registered with corresponding histological sections and analyzed. The internal elastic lamina was not identified in 52.6% of images. OFDI detected 60.2% of all calcifications identified histologically, with substantially higher detection rates for intimal than medial calcification (72.3% vs 30.8%). These findings indicate that OFDI provides acceptable assessment of intimal calcification but has limited capability for visualizing the medial layer in severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Recognition of these limitations may facilitate more appropriate pre-procedural planning for atherectomy in patients with severely calcified femoropopliteal disease.

articles.title: Balloon-occluded pulmonary arteriography and n-butyl cyanoacrylate embolization of angiographically occult pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysms.
articles.abstract: Angiographically occult pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysms - suspected on computed tomography but not shown at selective pulmonary angiography - have been presumed to have an occluded parent artery, and systemic-feeder embolization alone is often not curative. Three consecutive men with infection-related pseudoaneurysms presenting with massive hemoptysis were treated. In each, selective pulmonary angiography without occlusion showed proximal washout of injected contrast, consistent with reversed flow in the parent branch. The branch was occluded immediately proximal to the sac with a 4.0-mm microballoon - or, initially in one patient, a fortuitously wedged 5-F catheter - and hand injection under occlusion opacified the previously occult sac, which was then embolized with 25% n-butyl cyanoacrylate through a microballoon, without same-session systemic-artery embolization. All three achieved technical and clinical success, without recurrent hemoptysis over 17-22 months. Occultness does not equate to an occluded parent artery.

articles.title: In Vitro Development and Evaluation of an Endovascular Islet Cell Stent for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the in vitro development and benchtop evaluation of the IsletStent, an endovascular biologic stent-graft incorporating expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) semipermeable membranes, designed for portal venous delivery of pancreatic islets as a treatment for type 1 diabetes mellitus. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22 μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQ]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQ) islets. A benchtop normothermic perfusion circuit simulated intravascular deployment. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) was assessed in a repeated-measures design (n = 4 devices per experiment); murine islet-seeded devices were perfused under zero (0 mM), low (2.8 mM), and high (28 mM) glucose, and human islet-seeded devices under low and high glucose only, with insulin quantified by ELISA. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling under idealized, non-physiologic single-fluid conditions evaluated candidate device geometries. RESULTS: Murine islet-seeded devices demonstrated glucose-responsive insulin secretion: 3-hour insulin concentrations were 83 ± 8 vs. 145 ± 20 μIU/mL under low vs. high glucose (p = 0.02), and secretion rates were 5,344 ± 144 vs. 6,795 ± 503 μIU/hr (p = 0.008). Human islet-seeded devices responded concordantly, with 3-hour insulin concentrations of 229 ± 13 vs. 300 ± 17 μIU/mL (p = 0.014). CONCLUSION: In this benchtop perfusion model, islets housed within an ePTFE-based endovascular stent-graft retained glucose-responsive insulin secretion. In vivo evaluation of islet viability, direct immunoisolation, hemodynamic impact, and long-term function is required before clinical translation.

articles.title: Patient-Defined Experience in Venous-Origin Chronic Pelvic Pain: Conceptual Foundation for a Disease-Specific Patient-Reported Outcome Measure.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the symptoms, daily life impacts, and patient-defined meaningful treatment benefits of women with venous-origin chronic pelvic pain (VO-CPP), and to establish the conceptual basis for a disease-specific patient-reported outcome measure (PROM). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-one adult women with gynecologic pain specialist-confirmed VO-CPP underwent semi-structured concept elicitation interviews at seven U.S. CENTERS: Interviews explored symptoms, daily life impacts, and patient-defined meaningful treatment benefits. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis to develop a patient-centered conceptual model. RESULTS: No new impact concepts emerged after five interviews and no new symptom concepts after sixteen; five additional interviews confirmed saturation of symptom and impact concepts. Participants reported a broad symptom burden, with 76% describing ≥10 symptoms, and all reported impacts across at least three daily life domains. Although pelvic pain reduction was the most frequently identified meaningful treatment benefit, participants consistently defined meaningful improvement as restoration of daily functioning and valued activities rather than pain reduction alone. CONCLUSION: Women with VO-CPP experience a multidimensional disease burden extending well beyond pain intensity alone. Treatment outcomes assessment should incorporate patient-defined symptoms, daily life impacts, and meaningful benefits. These findings provide a patient-centered conceptual foundation for development of a VO-CPP PROM.

articles.title: ReCo-Diff: residual-conditioned deterministic sampling for cold diffusion in sparse-view CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reduces radiation dose andacquisition time but introduces structured streak artifacts that make reconstructionseverely ill-posed. Cold-diffusion approaches can model such deterministic degradationprocesses, but existing sampling strategies may rely on scalar similarity criteria andpredefined thresholds to trigger sample-adaptive resets of the degradation-level trajectory.We aim to replace this threshold-based sampling control with spatially resolved residualconditioning. APPROACH: We propose ReCo-Diff, a residual-conditioned cold-diffusionframework for sparse-view CT reconstruction. At each reverse step, a zero-residualbaseline prediction is re-degraded using the CT degradation operator, and the resultingsigned image-domain re-degradation discrepancy is used as a spatial conditioning map fora second restoration pass. ReCo-Diff does not require an adaptive reset duringresidual-conditioned sampling and instead follows a predetermined degradation schedule.A one-time level transition is additionally used for highly sparse inputs. The method wasevaluated on the AAPM Low-Dose CT dataset under 18-, 36-, and 72-view settings using apatient-wise split with one held-out test volume. MAIN RESULTS: ReCo-Diff achievedPSNR values of 38.54, 42.57, and 46.98 dB at 18, 36, and 72 views, respectively. At 18views, matched-computation analysis showed that ReCo-Diff achieved 38.54 dB comparedwith 38.25 dB for a two-pass zero-residual control under the same 18-NFE budget. Aspatially shifted-residual control achieved 37.65 dB, indicating that effective residualconditioning benefits from spatial correspondence with the current degraded state.Significance. ReCo-Diff replaces adaptive trajectory control with step-wise spatialresidual conditioning in deterministic cold diffusion. Matched-computation analysis showsthat the reconstruction benefit depends on spatially aligned residual information ratherthan on the additional network evaluation alone. The proposed strategy provides analternative approach to controlling error propagation under a predetermined degradationschedule without relying on sample-adaptive reset decisions.

articles.title: DuDoTransGAN: Dual-Domain transformer based generative adversarial unsupervised network for metal artifact reduction in paired and unpaired CT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Metal artifacts from implants degrade CT image quality, while supervised metal artifact reduction (MAR) methods require paired clean data that are rarely available clinically. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we developed DuDoTransGAN, an unsupervised dual-domain generative adversarial network for paired and unpaired training. It was evaluated on a publicly available paired synthetic dataset (SYN; 90,000 training and 2,000 test slices) and a clinical unpaired knee CT dataset (KNE; 19,032 slices from 66 patients; mean age, 55.8 ± 16.1 years; 36 males), including 6,168 slices with metal artifacts. On KNE, two radiologists independently assessed five image-quality aspects using Likert scales, with ratings reviewed by a senior radiologist. RESULTS: In the paired SYN experiment, DuDoTransGAN achieved a mean PSNR of 38.19 dB, the highest mean SSIM (0.975), and the lowest mean RMSE (5.65) among unsupervised methods. Performance remained stable with increasing metal-mask size, demonstrating robustness under larger-metal-mask conditions. In the unpaired KNE experiment, inter-rater agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.941). DuDoTransGAN achieved the highest mean scores among unsupervised methods for artifact removal (3.87 ± 0.48), diagnostic value (3.75 ± 0.50), visual effect (3.90 ± 0.36), and detail retention (3.96 ± 0.40), together with a comparable sharpness score (3.87 ± 0.58), and the highest radiologist selection rate (45 % vs 2 %-21 %). CONCLUSION: DuDoTransGAN is an adaptable unsupervised dual-domain MAR framework that performs effectively on paired synthetic and unpaired clinical data, producing high-quality, clinically interpretable CT images in the presence of metallic implants.

articles.title: Primary leiomyosarcoma arising adjacent to a femoral stem following total hip arthroplasty: a case report with radiologic and histopathological correlation.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic sarcomas associated with total hip arthroplasty (THA) are exceedingly rare, and most reported cases represent undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma or osteosarcoma. Primary leiomyosarcoma of bone is also an uncommon malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of primary malignant bone tumors. The occurrence of primary leiomyosarcoma adjacent to an orthopedic implant is therefore exceptionally rare. A 69-year-old woman presented with progressive left thigh pain 13 years after THA. Radiographs demonstrated osteolysis and cortical thinning at the distal femoral stem. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed an intramedullary lesion with cortical thinning and contrast enhancement. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-CT showed increased uptake at the lesion (SUV max, 11.9), without evidence of other primary tumors. The differential diagnoses included implant-related osteolysis, infection, metastatic tumor, and primary bone tumor. An open biopsy was performed, and a diagnosis of pleomorphic sarcoma was made. Wide resection with proximal femoral replacement was performed. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of primary leiomyosarcoma of bone. Prominent lymphocytic infiltration and immunohistochemical findings, including p53 overexpression and partial loss of Rb expression, within the tumor, raise the possibility of chronic inflammation and associated molecular alterations as theoretical contributing factors to tumorigenesis. Periprosthetic sarcomas can mimic more common postoperative complications, making diagnosis challenging. Delayed diagnosis may adversely affect prognosis. This case highlights the importance of considering malignancy in atypical periprosthetic lesions and underscores the role of multimodality imaging and biopsy in achieving an accurate diagnosis.

articles.title: Case report: Bilateral infantile acromion fractures in the setting of congenital glenoid dysplasia.
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of a 5-week-old male who presented with isolated acromion fractures occurring bilaterally 10 days apart. As scapular fractures are a high-specificity fracture for abusive injury, these findings were concerning for child abuse. The patient was later diagnosed with congenital glenoid dysplasia. Given this diagnosis with an otherwise normal medical evaluation for physical abuse, this case was deemed indeterminate for abusive injury. The multidisciplinary team consensus was that the injuries were likely fractures resulting from restriction of normal range of glenohumeral motion caused by his glenoid deformity. Literature on congenital glenoid dysplasia is limited in the pediatric population. This case highlights the need for further investigation into early presentations of congenital glenoid dysplasia and its association with acromion fractures.

articles.title: Associations between tissue stiffness, tumor response to transarterial chemoembolization and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: insights from multifrequency 3D-magnetic resonance elastography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the correlation between tissue stiffness, as measured across various target tissues using multifrequency three-dimensional magnetic resonance elastography (3D-MRE), and tumor responses to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), as well as post-treatment prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: HCC patients scheduled for TACE treatment were prospectively recruited and received multifrequency 3D-MRE before the initiation of TACE procedure. Measurements of tumor stiffness (TS), liver stiffness (LS), and spleen stiffness (SS) were conducted at frequencies of 60 Hz and 30 Hz, respectively. Treatment response was assessed using the mRECIST. Patient follow-up was conducted to evaluate overall survival outcomes. RESULTS: The final patient cohort consisted of 43 patients (mean age: 56.66±10.13 years; 34 males), including 16 non-responders and 27 responders. Non-responders exhibited significantly elevated TS (4.10±2.54 vs. 2.68±1.61kPa, p=0.035), LS (2.88±1.43 vs. 1.97±0.59kPa, p=0.026), and SS (4.03±0.90 vs. 3.13±1.08kPa, p=0.008) at the frequency of 30Hz. Firth's penalized univariable logistic analysis identified age (adjusted odds ratio [OR]=0.93, P=0.036), tumor number (OR=0.69, P=0.035), LS at 60Hz (OR=0.79, p=0.046), TS at 30Hz (OR=0.73, p=0.037), LS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, p=0.008), and SS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, P=0.009) as potential predictors of treatment response. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for predicting treatment response was 0.69 for age, tumor number and TS at 30Hz, 0.67 for LS at both 60Hz and 30Hz, and 0.75 for SS at 30Hz. Univariable Cox regression identified TS at both 60Hz (hazard ratio=1.15, p=0.014) and 30Hz (hazard ratio=1.40, p=0.010) as potential predictors of overall survival. CONCLUSION: Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

articles.title: Quantifying the Role of Interventional Radiology in Managing Patients with Hepatobiliary Cancers.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify the role of interventional radiology (IR) in managing primary and secondary hepatobiliary cancers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed administrative data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) using final action claims for Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries from 2016 to 2021. Patients aged ≥65 years with hepatobiliary cancer were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD), 10th Revision, codes. Services and associated work Relative Value Units (wRVUs) provided by IR, medical oncology, radiation oncology, and surgical oncology were identified using CMS physician specialty codes. IR procedures were classified as therapeutic or supportive. RESULTS: From 2016 to 2021, the Medicare hepatobiliary cancer cohort included 108,317-111,761 patients annually (mean age, 75 years; male, 53%). Medical oncologists treated 70% of patients, followed by interventional radiologists with 51%, radiation oncologists with 13%, and surgical oncologists with 5%. Physician service volumes and wRVU remained stable, with medical oncologists providing the largest share (69% of services and 13.7% of wRVUs), followed by interventional radiologists (2.9% and 11.7%, respectively), radiation oncologists (1.3% and 4.5%, respectively), and surgical oncologists (0.1% and 2.2%, respectively). Interventional radiologists performed 75,785 therapeutic procedures, primarily for hepatocellular carcinoma (59%). Before pandemic, IR volumes increased 57%, driven by liver ablations (+25%) and supportive services (+63%), whereas transarterial therapies declined slightly (-6%). Despite the drop in volume during the pandemic, IR saw the highest compound annual growth rate (4%) among the specialties analyzed. CONCLUSIONS: IR provides a substantial share of services for patients with hepatobiliary cancers, with rising use of therapeutic and supportive services, delivering similar wRVUs at lower costs, underscoring its growing role in cancer care.

articles.title: How do Uncompensated Micro-Shifts Systematically Confound Low-Concentration Metabolite Quantification in 1H-MRS Analysis?
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Linear combination model fitting is widely used for spectral analysis in 1H-MRS but relies on basis sets with fixed spin-system parameters, implicitly neglecting the sensitivity of chemical shifts to physiological and pathological tissue microenvironments. This study systematically evaluated the impact of frequency perturbations on spectral analysis and reassessed the validity of the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) as a quality-control metric for low-concentration metabolites. METHODS: The effects of frequency perturbations on spectral analysis were investigated using simulated datasets with different baseline models and lineshapes, followed by validation in a publicly available in vivo human brain 1H-MRS dataset (n = 31). Estimated metabolite concentrations, relative concentration changes, estimation errors, and CRLB values were analyzed across all conditions. RESULTS: Frequency perturbations produced minimal quantification changes in high-concentration metabolites but substantially larger errors in several low-concentration metabolites. Across both simulations and in vivo validation, relative concentration changes generally remained below 3% for high-concentration metabolites but exceeded 10%-20% for several low-concentration metabolites, including Gln, GSH, Asp, and NAAG. Importantly, substantial estimation errors frequently occurred despite CRLB values remaining within conventionally acceptable ranges. These findings were consistently observed across different baseline models, lineshapes, and in vivo validation. CONCLUSION: Physiologically relevant frequency perturbations can introduce substantial quantification bias that is not consistently reflected by CRLB. These findings identify environmentally induced resonance-frequency variations as an underrecognized source of quantification error in current linear-combination model fitting and suggest that CRLB alone is insufficient for assessing quantification reliability, particularly under conditions associated with altered brain temperature or tissue pH.

articles.title: In Vivo Dynamic D2O-MRI for Quantifying Apparent CSF Water Renewal Across Ventricular and Extraventricular Compartments.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The choroid plexus has long been regarded as the principal source of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), yet this view remains unresolved. We developed a dynamic indirect D2O MRI approach to quantify regional apparent CSF water renewal in vivo in rats at 9.4 T. METHODS: Rats were scanned at 9.4 T using spin-echo echo-planar imaging during intravenous D2O infusion (10.69-s temporal resolution, 150 × 150 μm2 in-plane resolution). A deliberately long echo time (TE = 150 ms) was used to preferentially suppress signals from brain parenchyma, blood, and interstitial fluid, thereby enhancing sensitivity to signal changes in CSF compartments. After relaxation correction, regional apparent CSF water renewal rates were estimated using a one-compartment kinetic model. RESULTS: D2O-induced signal attenuation was regionally heterogeneous. The ambient and supracerebellar cisterns (AC + SC) exhibited the largest signal reduction, reaching 47.32% ± 15.70% of baseline, whereas the lateral ventricles (LVs) showed smaller reductions (LV1: 68.73% ± 18.72%; LV2: 72.64% ± 15.07%). The estimated apparent CSF water renewal rates were low and comparable between the bilateral ventricles (LV1: 0.20 ± 0.20 μL/min; LV2: 0.26 ± 0.21 μL/min), but markedly higher in the AC + SC region (4.38 ± 3.95 μL/min; p < 0.01 vs. LVs). The third and fourth ventricles also showed relatively small signal changes. CONCLUSION: Dynamic D2O MRI enabled noninvasive assessment of apparent CSF water renewal in vivo. The total apparent renewal rate was higher in AC + SC than in the LVs. These results suggest that extraventricular CSF compartments contribute substantially to apparent CSF water renewal.

articles.title: Depiction Fidelity and Specificity in Direct MRI of Collagen: Addressing Signal Decay at the Microsecond Timescale.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Gap-filled zero echo time (ZTE) acquisitions combined with dedicated short-T2 hardware enable direct collagen imaging on the timescale of macromolecular (MM) signals, with T2s ˜ 10 μs. However, present methods offer limited depiction fidelity, and their specificity towards MM content is poorly understood. This work presents methodology to improve depiction fidelity of MM signals and investigates how imaging parameters influence MM specificity. METHODS: 1D simulations of gap-filled ZTE sequences acquiring MM signals are used to evaluate depiction fidelity and specificity via the modulation transfer function (MTF) and point spread function (PSF). Insights are used to address signal decay at the microsecond timescale by (i) modifying the k-space sampling pattern through gap filling with MTF smoothing, (ii) selecting acquisition parameters that optimize MM specificity and (iii) designing a post-processing filter to improve resolution. The approaches are demonstrated with 3D imaging simulations and experiments. RESULTS: Gap-filled ZTE with specialized hardware targets MM signals but enters a unique imaging regime where depiction fidelity is limited: the PSF exhibits a broad main lobe from T2 blurring and far-reaching side lobes caused by a kink in the k-space sampling pattern. The latter is addressed through MTF smoothing. MM specificity is then maximized by subtracting two images acquired at different times but maintaining imaging bandwidth. Finally, post-processing filters narrow MM PSF main lobe, reducing T2 blurring and improving depiction fidelity. CONCLUSION: The investigation and developed methods improve collagen MM imaging, with potential applications for in vivo imaging or assessing materials that exhibit decay on MM timescales.

articles.title: Musculoskeletal MRI Relaxometry Phantom for T1, T2, and T1ρ Measurements.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Quantitative MRI (qMRI) requires quality assurance methods that reflect in vivo conditions to ensure consistent measurements with low bias and high reproducibility over time, across multiple sites, and across different MRI scanner manufacturers and models. PURPOSE: To develop a musculoskeletal (MSK) relaxometry phantom that spans the T1 and T2 (and T1ρ as an exploratory aim) ranges of articular cartilage. STUDY TYPE: Longitudinal phantom study. PHANTOM: A cylindrical phantom designed to fit within multiple knee coil configurations using dedicated support stands. The phantom contains 12 gel-filled vials spanning T1 values of 300-1200 ms, T2 values of 10-100 ms, and T1ρ values of 20-120 ms, and an MR-visible thermometer. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3T; single-echo spin-echo T2; inversion-recovery T1; spin-lock prepared T1ρ for NMR (spin-lock frequencies 300-5000 Hz) and MAPSS T1ρ for MRI (spin-lock frequency 500 Hz). ASSESSMENT: NMR and two MRI systems from different vendors were used. A prototype phantom (n = 1), production phantoms (n = 12), and matched NMR samples were evaluated. NMR data acquired at multiple temperatures served as reference and enabled temperature correction of MRI measurements. The prototype phantom was scanned longitudinally (15 measurements over 725 days) to assess stability, while production phantoms were scanned at a single timepoint to evaluate batch consistency. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Measurement variability and agreement were assessed using coefficients of variation (CVs), concordance correlation coefficients (CCCs), and Bland-Altman analysis for NMR-MRI comparison, longitudinal stability, batch consistency, and inter-vendor reproducibility. RESULTS: After temperature correction, longitudinal CVs were 1.1% (T1), 1.8% (T2), and 1.6% (T1ρ). Production phantoms showed inter-phantom CVs of 0.8% (T1), 1.2% (T2), and 0.9% (T1ρ). NMR and MRI measurements demonstrated strong agreement (CCCs > 0.99 for T1, T2, and T1ρ) with biases < 6%. Inter-vendor MRI comparisons yielded CCCs > 0.99 for T1 and T2. DATA CONCLUSION: The phantom demonstrated excellent stability and reproducibility with temperature correction, supporting its use for quality assurance in longitudinal and multisite qMRI studies. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 1. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 1.

articles.title: Systematic review of spectral computed tomography quantitative parameters for predicting EGFR mutation status in non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene mutations are important therapeutic targets in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Spectral computed tomography (spectral CT) has shown promise in the non-invasive prediction of EGFR status; however, the diagnostic value of these parameters remains unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the utility of key quantitative spectral CT parameters for predicting EGFR mutation status in NSCLC. METHODS: A comprehensive search of several Chinese and English databases was conducted to retrieve relevant diagnostic studies published up to October 1, 2025 that used pathology as the gold standard to assess the predictive value of spectral CT quantitative parameters for EGFR mutation detection in NSCLC. Two researchers conducted the literature screening and data extraction independently. Due to study heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. RESULTS: The quantitative parameters of spectral CT, including iodine concentration (IC), normalized iodine concentration (NIC), slope of the spectral Hounsfield unit curve (λHU), and effective atomic number (Zeff), were higher in the EGFR-mutant cohort than in the wild-type cohort (P<0.05). Multi-parameter models combining quantitative parameters with clinical and imaging features showed improved diagnostic performance. The results were unaffected by the various brands of CT scanners and their scanning parameters. CONCLUSIONS: Several quantitative parameters derived from spectral CT are associated with EGFR mutations in NSCLC. Predictive models integrating these quantitative parameters with imaging features and clinical variables may further improve diagnostic efficacy. This may inform epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) planing. Large-scale prospective studies are needed to validate these models.

articles.title: Deep learning-based segmentation, grading and genotype classification of glioma: a literature analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Glioma represents the most prevalent and lethal primary brain tumor in adults, and its high mortality poses a significant challenge to clinical decision-making. While the conventional gold standard for diagnosis relies on the examination of surgically resected tumor tissue, recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have demonstrated compelling performance in medical image analysis, offering the potential for non-invasive prediction of the genetic and histological features of glioma as well as automatic tumor segmentation. This review aims to comprehensively summarize deep learning-based techniques for glioma segmentation, grading, and genotype classification. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) Xplore, and Scopus for articles published in English between January 2014 and December 2025, using combinations of the terms "glioma", "brain tumor", "deep learning", "convolutional neural network", "segmentation", "classification", "grading", "genotype", "isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)", "1p/19q", and "O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT)". Peer-reviewed studies that applied deep learning methods to glioma analysis using medical imaging data and reported quantitative performance results were included, whereas review articles without original results, studies using exclusively non-deep-learning methods, and studies focused solely on non-glioma brain tumors were excluded. KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: This review first summarizes the commonly used public datasets [Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS), The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), synthetic, and private cohorts] and performance metrics, and then surveys deep learning-based approaches for glioma segmentation, grading, and genotype classification according to task. Recent methodological advances, including Vision Transformers, foundation models such as the segment anything model (SAM) and MedSAM, diffusion models, and self-supervised learning, are also discussed. Reported performance varies considerably across datasets and evaluation protocols, and risks of bias, including slice-level data leakage, patient overlap across public repositories, and single-center confounding, remain prevalent in the genotype prediction literature. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning has become a transformative tool for non-invasive glioma characterization. Future research should prioritize prospective multi-center validation, standardized evaluation protocols, calibrated uncertainty estimation, and clinically deployable frameworks, thereby facilitating the translation of these techniques into routine diagnostic workflows and ultimately improving outcomes for patients with glioma.

articles.title: Incremental prognostic value of left atrial minimum volume index and late gadolinium enhancement in acute myocardial infarction patients with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤35.
articles.abstract: AIM: Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤35% are at high risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). The left atrial minimum volume index (LAVImin) and late gadolinium enhancement of the left ventricular myocardium (LGE) have each been reported as stand-alone predictors, but their combined risk stratification and incremental prognostic value in this specific population remains unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-centre study included 338 patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% (training cohort, n = 235; external validation cohort, n = 103) imaged by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) between January 2014 and October 2024. Two blinded radiologists quantified LAVImin, LGE, and other CMR parameters. Cox regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis evaluated the separate and combined prognostic value of LAVImin and LGE. Five nested prediction models were developed and validated internally and externally. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 37 months, 55 of 235 training cohort patients (23.4%) experienced MACE. Patients with LAVImin ≥20.4 mL/m2 and LGE ≥29.5% had the poorest MACE-free survival (log-rank P < .001). The model combining clinical factors, conventional CMR risk factors, LAVImin and LGE (Model 5) discriminated best (apparent Harrell C statistic 0.77, optimism-corrected 0.73; external validation 0.78, calibration slope 0.96) and improved modestly but significantly on the conventional CMR model (Model 2; likelihood ratio P < .001, ΔAUC = 0.051, P = .04). CONCLUSION: In patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% who underwent CMR, combined LAVImin and LGE enable survival risk stratification and provide modest but significant incremental prognostic value for MACE.

articles.title: Machine learning for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases and non-small cell lung cancer histological subtype classification: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: AIM: This study aimed to systematically review machine learning (ML) methods applied to computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET)/CT for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases and for lung cancer histological subtype classification. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched for original peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to May 31, 2026. Eligible studies applied ML, deep learning, or radiomics to CT, PET, or PET/CT for primary versus metastatic lung lesion differentiation or major lung cancer histological subtype classification. Methodological quality was assessed with Quality assessment of comparative diagnostic accuracy studies (QUADAS-2), and reporting was evaluated using 10 prespecified Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging-aligned items. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies were included after eligibility reassessment. Twenty-one provided a numeric study-level Area Under the Curve (AUC); the median representative AUC was 0.889 (IQR 0.820-0.936). The median AUC was 0.923 for primary/metastatic differentiation and 0.874 for histological subtype classification. Only 5 of 22 studies (22.7%) used independent external testing; among 4 externally validated studies with numeric AUCs, the median was 0.720. QUADAS-2 showed frequent uncertainty in patient selection (17/22, 77.3%), while CLAIM-aligned assessment identified limited external testing, code/model availability (3/22, 13.6%), and explainability reporting (4/22, 18.2%). CONCLUSION: CT- and PET/CT-based ML models show promising diagnostic performance for lung lesion-origin and histological subtype classification, but performance is lower in independent external evaluation. Broader multicentre validation, transparent reporting, reproducible code/model access, and prospective assessment are required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer: a proof-of-concept comparison with primary-tumor radiomics.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colorectal cancer remains challenging using conventional CT assessment. This proof-of-concept study compared CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics with primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative prediction of LNM. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients with pathologically confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced CT and surgical resection. Patients were divided into training and validation cohorts. Radiomics features were extracted from the primary tumor and visible regional lymph nodes across multiple nodal stations. Three radiomics strategies were developed and compared: primary-tumor radiomics, multi-station lymph-node radiomics, and combined radiomics. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and five-fold cross-validation. Pairwise AUCs were compared using the DeLong test. A clinical-radiomic model was further constructed by integrating the optimal radiomics strategy with preoperative clinical variables. RESULTS: In the validation cohort, the multi-station lymph-node radiomics model outperformed the primary-tumor radiomics model for predicting LNM (AUC, 0.864 versus 0.637; p = 0.0055). The combined radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.840, without significant improvement over the lymph-node model (p = 0.2211). After integration with clinical variables, the clinical-radiomic model achieved an AUC of 0.879. CONCLUSION: CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics showed significantly higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative LNM prediction in colorectal cancer. However, this single-center proof-of-concept model is not ready for direct clinical implementation and requires multicenter external validation before clinical translation. KEY POINTS: Question Can CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics improve preoperative nodal metastasis prediction beyond primary-tumor radiomics in patients with surgically treated colorectal cancer? Findings Multi-station lymph-node radiomics achieved higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level prediction of pathological lymph-node metastasis in colorectal cancer. Relevance statement CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics may support individualized preoperative nodal risk stratification in colorectal cancer, but multicenter validation and prospective evaluation are required before clinical translation.

articles.title: Phase-adaptive automated whole-liver quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices from gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a phase-adaptive pipeline for automated whole-liver, parenchyma-based quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices from gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI without inter-phase co-registration. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center study (2016-2025), 9,013 liver MRI examinations were screened, and 3,112 gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI examinations were identified. The first examination per patient defined the clinical cohort (1,174 patients; mean age, 59.6 ± 14 years [range, 4-93 years]; 611 men). A phase-adaptive nnU-Net was trained on 403 and tested on 500 dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI sequences for segmentation of liver parenchyma, intrahepatic non-parenchymal structures, and spleen; paraspinal muscle reference regions were obtained using TotalSegmentator. Segmentation accuracy was assessed against manually corrected reference segmentations generated by a semi-automatic annotation workflow with Dice similarity coefficients. Automated arterial enhancement fraction (AEF), relative liver enhancement (RLE), hepatocellular uptake index (HUI), liver-to-spleen ratio (LSR), and liver-to-muscle ratio (LMR) were compared with manual region-of-interest measurements in a radiological validation cohort (50 patients) using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Liver indices were compared between patients with cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic livers using the Mann-Whitney U-test. RESULTS: Liver parenchyma segmentation achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.998-0.999. Reader-model agreement for the liver indices ranged from 0.936 to 0.977. HUI, LSR, RLE, and LMR were lower in cirrhosis (p < 0.001), whereas AEF did not differ (p = 0.14). CONCLUSION: Phase-adaptive segmentation enables whole-liver quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices without inter-phase co-registration. The lower hepatobiliary uptake indices in cirrhosis support the plausibility of this approach for scalable quantitative assessment of liver MRI. KEY POINTS: Question Can gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI be quantified automatically across contrast phases without inter-phase co-registration or manual region-of-interest placement in routine clinical imaging? Findings Phase-adaptive segmentation enabled automated whole-liver quantification with liver Dice coefficients of 0.998-0.999 and excellent agreement with manual measurements for five liver indices. Relevance Statement Automated whole-liver quantification from standard gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI provides reproducible, signal-intensity-derived liver indices and reduces dependence on manual region-of-interest measurements in large-scale clinical studies.

articles.title: Evaluation of iodine detection and quantification limits in photon-counting CT-a phantom study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Clinical decisions using CT iodine maps are based on evaluation of contrast enhancement, making it essential to understand how accurately CT systems detect and quantify iodine, yet quantitative evaluations remain scarce, and few studies treat iodine as an analyte for which detection threshold, quantification precision, and measurement linearity can be determined using standard laboratory-science concepts. No study has applied such concepts across photon-counting CT (PCCT) and dual-energy CT (DECT) systems. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using head and abdominal protocols, test tubes with iodine concentrations (0.0-2.0 mg/mL) were placed in a phantom providing head- and abdomen-equivalent attenuation. Scans were performed at two dose levels per protocol, on two DECT and one PCCT system. Iodine images were reconstructed for repeated scans using varying iterative reconstruction (IR) levels. Limit-of-detection (LoD), limit-of-quantification (LoQ), and lower-limit-of-linear-interval (LLLI) were calculated for two ROI sizes (3 and 10 mm), and differences between scanners were analyzed with Welch ANOVA and Games-Howell tests (α = 0.05). RESULTS: PCCT demonstrated significantly lower LoD/LoQ values than the DECT systems across most protocols. For low-dose abdomen (3 mGy, medium-IR), LoD for 3 and 10 mm ROI size were 0.78 and 0.16 mg/mL (PCCT), 1.28 and 0.26 mg/mL (split-filter CT), and 1.42 and 0.57 mg/mL (dual-source CT). LoQ values were also lower for PCCT. Improvements were most pronounced in low-dose protocols, with LoD reductions up to 68% (brain) and 45% (abdomen). LLLI was similar across systems. CONCLUSION: PCCT outperformed DECT in iodine detection and quantification, particularly in low-dose protocols. These findings highlight the potential use of reduced iodine contrast and/or radiation dose. KEY POINTS: Question Objective comparison of iodine detection and quantification performance between PCCT and DECT systems remains limited, particularly for low-iodine contrast media doses. Findings PCCT achieved significantly lower detection and quantification thresholds than conventional CT systems, particularly for small lesions and low-dose imaging protocols. Relevance statement Task-based LoD and LoQ metrics enable objective comparison of CT system performance and may provide clinically relevant thresholds for iodine detectability, quantification, and protocol optimization.

Nomogram models integrating multiregion radiomics, quantitative computed tomography, and clinical indicators for distinguishing connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and improving the prediction of gender-age-physiology stage.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), along with assessment of the interstitial lung disease gender-age-physiology (ILD-GAP) index, is crucial for formulating effective therapeutic interventions. The aim of this study was to examine whether multiregion radiomics combined with clinical indicators and quantitative computed tomography (QCT) can enhance the diagnostic accuracy for IPF and CTD-ILD. We also assessed the potential of radiomics as a noninvasive alternative to pulmonary function testing (PFT) for evaluating ILD-GAP staging, a prognostic marker. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with IPF and CTD-ILD at two centers. Honeycombing (H), reticulation (R), and ground-glass opacity (GGO) were outlined in representative regions, and radiomics features were then extracted. Multidimensional data included multiregional radiomics, QCT (lesion volume), and clinical indicators. The most appropriate machine learning algorithms were selected to develop models. Ultimately, the logistic regression algorithm was employed to establish a nomogram model for distinguishing IPF from CTD-ILD and a nomogram gender-age-physiology (nomogram-GAP) model for predicting ILD-GAP staging. Model performance was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: To differentiate IPF from CTD-ILD, we enrolled patients from Center A into training (n=153), test (n=64), and internal validation (n=42) sets, as well as 40 patients from Center B into an external validation set. The nomogram model yielded an AUC of 0.854 in the internal validation set and 0.823 in the external validation set. For ILD-GAP staging prediction, Center A patients were split into training (n=155) and internal validation sets (n=31). The nomogram-GAP model had an AUC of 0.881 in the internal validation set. Calibration and DCA demonstrated that the nomogram model and nomogram-GAP model exhibit strong consistency and clinical utility. CONCLUSIONS: Two types of nomograms integrating multiregion radiomics, QCT, and clinical indicators demonstrated promising performance in distinguishing IPF from CTD-ILD and predicting ILD-GAP staging. When PFTs are unreliable or impracticable, the nomogram-GAP model may serve as a reliable marker for assessing ILD-GAP staging.

articles.title: Prediction of patient-specific quality assurance for volumetric modulated arc therapy using machine log files.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep learning (DL) models have been used for predicting gamma passing rates (GPRs) of patient specific quality assurance (PSQA) in volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). As the model input mostly from planning parameters and dose distribution, the effect of motion precision of the treatment machine has frequently been ignored. In this study,the most recent motion precision of multi-leaf collimator (MLC) leaves was estimated by their records in machine log file and used jointly with the beam intensity map to predict GPRs of VMAT PSQA. METHODS: The input of the DL model consists of two parts: the MLC positional error map which was estimated from machine log file and the beam intensity map which was obtained from the treatment plan. A UNet++ model was trained to predict the GPR of VMAT PSQA. The effect of feature maps and time intervals in estimating MLC leaf positional error maps on the prediction accuracy was evaluated. In addition, the proposed model was compared with two competing DL models (ResNet and SE-Net) and a classic regression model. The prediction error was quantified by mean absolute errors (MAEs) under two clinical accepted criteria (3%-3 mm and 3%-2 mm). Pearson's correlation coefficient (r) between measured and predicted GPR was also assessed. RESULTS: The model with the inputs of beam intensity and MLC leaf positional error maps achieved the best performance among all combinations with various input feature maps. The MAEs predicted by the proposed model with MLC leaf positional error map obtained from 5 days' records were 0.90 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 1.74 for 3%-2 mm criterion, whereas those predicted by the proposed model with MLC leaf positional error map obtained from 1 day's record were 1.01 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 1.85 for 3%-2 mm criterion. The proposed model achieved the smaller MAEs (1.01 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 1.85 for 3%-2 mm criterion) than the other two competing models: ResNet (2.85 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 2.83 for 3%-2 mm criterion) and SE-Net (3.53 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 4.55 for 3%-2 mm criterion). CONCLUSIONS: The proposed model that combines beam intensity map and MLC leaf positional error map exhibited a better prediction performance for GPRs of VMAT PSQA. It would be advantageous to include more motion precision information of treatment machine into DL models for high-performance prediction of VMAT PSQA.

articles.title: Nodule subtype dependency of CT-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of spread through air spaces in stage I lung adenocarcinoma: a multi-centre study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Spread through air spaces (STAS) is an important invasive pattern associated with aggressive behaviour and prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma. However, whether nodule subtype influences the performance of computed tomography (CT)-based radiomics for preoperative STAS prediction remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of nodule subtype on CT-based radiomics performance for STAS prediction in stage I lung adenocarcinoma. METHODS: This was a multi-centre retrospective study, with 1,377 patients in the internal cohort and 436 in the external validation cohorts. Two radiomics models were developed: an all-subtype model (M1) and a pure-solid-specific model (M2). Radiomic features were obtained from preoperative CT images, and model development was performed using Extreme Gradient Boosting. Predictive performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration analysis, and decision-curve analysis. In the external pure-solid cohort, the two models were directly compared using the DeLong test, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). RESULTS: M1 yielded an AUC of 0.839 in the internal cohort and 0.865 in the overall external cohort. After external stratification by nodule subtype, the AUCs for non-solid and pure-solid nodules were 0.797 and 0.788, respectively. M2 yielded an AUC of 0.773 in the internal cohort and 0.768 in the external cohort. In the external pure-solid cohort, M1 exhibited superior discrimination (P=0.0018), while M2 yielded more favourable reclassification performance (NRI =0.643; IDI =0.184). CONCLUSIONS: CT-based radiomics may have value for preoperative STAS prediction; however, its predictive performance likely depends on nodule subtype, with pure-solid nodules representing the primary diagnostic challenge.

articles.title: The utility of patient symptom questionnaires in CT of the lumbosacral spine.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower back pain and radiculopathy impose significant burdens on healthcare systems. Computed tomography (CT) scans are often used as an imaging modality for lower back symptomatology in the community. Accurately identifying relevant symptom sources using CT scans is often challenging due to the high incidence of incidental structural abnormalities. We examine the effectiveness of patient questionnaires in assisting reporting of CT scans of the lumbosacral spine. METHODS: In this retrospective audit, a questionnaire was provided to 250 consecutive patients undergoing lumbar spine CT prior to their scan being reported. Questions addressed the type of symptoms, such as pain and/or altered sensation, the location of these, and previous investigations. These questionnaires were provided with the lumbar spine CT scans, which were then reported by a pool of 30 radiologists. RESULTS: Of the 250 questionnaires administered, one was excluded from analysis as peer-review feedback identified inconsistency with the inclusion criteria. Of the 249, 214 questionnaires were completed and included for further analysis. Of the 214 patients who completed the questionnaire, 211 of them had back pain (98.6%) whilst 3 (1.4%) did not. One hundred sixty-four (76.6%) patients had lumbar spine-related sensory symptoms (altered sensation or limb pain) whilst 50 (23.4%) did not. Of the 214 patients with completed questionnaires, 184 radiological reports referenced the questionnaires (86%), whereas 30 (14%) did not. Of the 214 patients, 33 (15.4%) had clinical request information that suggested alternate pathology to what was indicated on the questionnaire. In these 33 cases, 28 (84.8%) radiological reports made direct reference to the patient questionnaire. For the 164 patients with lumbar spine-related sensory symptoms, 24 (14.6%) had incongruent clinical request information with questionnaires. In these 24 cases, 19 (79.2%) had radiological reports which made reference to the questionnaire. For the 50 patients with lower back pain as their sole symptom, 9 (18%) had incongruent clinical request information with questionnaires. In all 9 (100%) of these cases, radiological reports referenced the questionnaires. The questionnaire identified that 199 out of 214 patients (93%) had external lower back imaging available. CONCLUSIONS: Inclusion of a symptom questionnaire has benefit to the reporting radiologist. We observed a high completion and usage rate of the questionnaire, which may indicate feasible use in regular workflows. Importantly, we noted that patient questionnaires help with providing accurate clinical information and are especially important for cases in which there are differing accounts of patient symptomatology, both for patients with lumbar spine-related sensory symptoms and for those with lower back pain as a sole symptom. Furthermore, they can inform radiologists when external lower back imaging is available. These factors can assist the radiologist in providing higher quality reports, ideally resulting in better patient outcomes.

articles.title: Possible hemodynamic mechanisms in the size change of cerebral aneurysms: an exploratory study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In asymptomatic small unruptured intracranial aneurysms (IAs), growth is one of the important factors determining treatment to prevent rupture and hemorrhage. Hemodynamic factors play a crucial role in the growth and regression of aneurysms, although the mechanisms involved are not yet clear. The aim of this study was to investigate the hemodynamic mechanisms underlying size changes in small unruptured IAs (<7 mm) during follow-up. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 63 patients with unruptured IAs (<7 mm) who underwent computed tomography angiography (CTA) imaging follow-up for more than 6 months. Aneurysm hemodynamic and morphological parameters were measured by software AneuFlow. Statistical comparisons were performed between enlarging aneurysms and stable aneurysms. RESULTS: Enlarging aneurysms (43/63, 68%) exhibited a significantly higher baseline wall shear stress (WSS) (7.98 vs. 5.76 Pa, P=0.04) and a borderline higher WSS gradient (WSSG) (9.83 vs. 5.62 Pa/mm, P=0.05) compared to stable aneurysms. During enlargement, WSSG decreased (P=0.04), while parent vessel diameter increased (P<0.01), accompanied by reduced parent vessel WSS (P<0.01). In 30% of growing cases, parent vessel expansion was correlated with marked WSS and WSSG reduction in the aneurysm, suggesting adaptive remodeling. Low normalized WSS (NWSS) was correlated with decrease in diameter of the parent vessel (Dvessel) (r=0.30, P=0.02) and aneurysm surface area (r=0.36, P<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: This study analyzed the effect of hemodynamics on the size change of aneurysms. High WSS and high WSSG may be inducing factors for aneurysm enlargement, while high WSS may lead to expansion of the parent vessel. In the early stages of aneurysm development, low WSS may contribute to size reduction.

articles.title: Predictive models for trans-stenotic pressure gradient in the transverse sinus based on multimodal correlates.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The invasive nature of the methods currently available for screening based on the trans-stenotic pressure gradient (TPG) limits their widespread application. We aimed to develop machine learning models for predicting TPG in the transverse sinus. METHODS: The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Beijing Friendship Hospital Affiliated to Capital Medical University. We retrospectively analyzed the data of 83 patients confirmed to have pressure-measured transverse sinus stenosis from January 2017 to June 2022 at Beijing Friendship Hospital. The dataset included clinical, laboratory, computed tomography angiography, and four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance data with 29 feature indicators. Six machine learning methods-support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, decision tree, random forest (RF), gradient boosting decision tree, and extreme gradient boosting-were employed to construct classification models for 4- and 8-mmHg TPG thresholds via fivefold cross-validation. Models were evaluated according to accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and area under the curve (AUC). RESULTS: For the 4-mmHg threshold, RF showed the highest performance, with an accuracy of 0.83, a specificity of 0.62, a sensitivity of 0.95, an F1 score of 0.92, an MCC of 0.60, and an AUC of 0.92. RF also excelled for the 8-mmHg threshold, with accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, F1 score, MCC, and AUC values of 0.84, 0.86, 0.81, 0.78, 0.70, and 0.91, respectively. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis indicated that peak velocity and average velocity differences positively correlated with TPG, whereas the residual area ratio was negatively correlated. CONCLUSIONS: The models demonstrated strong discriminative ability and are useful for noninvasive TPG prediction.

articles.title: Quantitative dual-energy computed tomography parameters as imaging biomarkers for assessing the histopathologic grade of colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global healthcare burden. Tumor differentiation grade is a critical prognostic factor for evaluating patients with CRC. The objective of this study was to examine the value of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) quantitative parameters as imaging biomarkers for the preoperative prediction of histopathologic CRC grade. METHODS: A total of 117 patients with pathologically confirmed CRC who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced DECT were enrolled and divided into low-grade (n=74) and high-grade (n=43) groups. Monoenergetic 74-keV images from the arterial phase (AP), venous phase (VP), and delayed phase (DP) were reconstructed as conventional 120 kVp-like computed tomography (CT) images. Lesion CT attenuation values, iodine concentration (IC), normalized iodine concentration (NIC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and extracellular volume (ECV) were measured in three phases by two radiologists, and clinical data were collected. Intergroup comparisons and Spearman correlation analyses were conducted to determine the associations between spectral parameters and the histopathologic grade of CRC, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were applied to identify independent correlates. Three types of predictive models were established: a baseline model incorporating clinical variables and CT attenuation values, a single spectral parameter model, and combined models integrating clinical features with different spectral parameters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and the DeLong test were used to compare the area under the curve (AUC) between the models. Bootstrap internal validation with 1,000 resamples was performed on the optimal model. RESULTS: Serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) concentration showed significant differences between the low-grade group and high-grade group (P=0.009), whereas triphasic 120 kVp-like CT attenuation values showed no statistical differences (P>0.05). For the AP, only IC differed significantly (P=0.011); for the VP and DP, IC, NIC, Zeff, and ECV differed significantly (P<0.05), with ECV showing the strongest correlation with histopathologic grade in CRC (r=0.650: P<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified VP IC [odds ratio (OR) =4.601; P=0.046] and ECV (OR =1.492; P<0.001) as independent correlates of high histopathologic grade in CRC, with AUCs of 0.749 and 0.889, respectively. The integrated model combining clinical indicators with VP and DP spectral parameters achieved the best performance for predicting high histopathologic grade in CRC [AUC =0.904, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.845-0.962; bias‑corrected AUC =0.904, 95% CI: 0.837-0.954], with an accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of 85.5%, 88.4%, and 83.8%, respectively. The DeLong test revealed that this integrated model had significantly better diagnostic performance than did the baseline model (AUC =0.538; P<0.001), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed between the integrated model and the VP + DP dual-phase model (P=0.504). CONCLUSIONS: DECT quantitative parameters have potential clinical value for predicting the histopathologic grade of patients with CRC. They may serve as imaging biomarkers and provide valuable information for understanding tumor biological behavior.

articles.title: Diagnostic value of a multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging-based nomogram incorporating apparent diffusion coefficient in preoperative differentiation of phyllodes tumors from breast cancer: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preoperative differentiation between phyllodes tumors (PTs) and breast cancers (BCs) remains a clinical challenge due to their overlapping imaging characteristics. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), incorporating morphological, hemodynamic, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) parameters, to develop a nomogram model for differentiating PTs from BCs, and to preliminarily explore the association between ADC parameters and the histologic grade of PTs. METHODS: A total of 92 patients (mean age, 46.04 years) with pathologically confirmed PTs (n=31) or BCs (n=61) who underwent 3.0 Tesla (T) breast MRI at the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between June 2018 and June 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. Multiparametric MRI features, including morphological characteristics, hemodynamic parameters, and quantitative diffusion metrics [mean ADC (ADCmean) and relative ADC (rADC)], were assessed for all lesions. Intergroup differences were compared using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, independent samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Mann-Whitney U test or Kruskal-Wallis H test, Chi-squared test, or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors and construct a diagnostic nomogram. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, decision curve analysis (DCA), and calibration curve analysis. Finally, 5-fold internal cross-validation was used to assess the model's stability. RESULTS: PTs were characterized predominantly by a lobulated morphology, hyperintensity on T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and T2 hypointense septations, whereas BCs typically presented as irregular masses with spiculated margins and peritumoral edema.
