Regarding dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) features, PTs predominantly demonstrated rapid initial enhancement with heterogeneous or dark internal septations, and time-intensity curves (TICs) mainly exhibited Type I/II patterns. PTs demonstrated significantly higher ADCmean, rADC1 (lesion-to-pectoralis muscle ratio), and rADC2 (lesion-to-contralateral gland ratio) values compared with the BCs (all P<0.001). Subgroup analysis revealed a stepwise decrease in ADCmean from benign PTs to borderline/malignant PTs and BCs. The diagnostic nomogram integrating T2WI signal intensity, T2 hypointense septations, TIC pattern, and ADCmean achieved an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.997. Following rigorous internal 5-fold cross-validation with Firth's penalty to mitigate potential overfitting, the model maintained a robust average AUC of 0.978 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.951-1.000]. DCA demonstrated the net clinical benefit of the combined model. CONCLUSIONS: Multiparametric MRI provides significant diagnostic value in preoperatively differentiating PTs from BCs. Although the subgroup analysis regarding PT histological grading remains preliminary due to limited sample sizes, both ADCmean and rADC offer valuable quantitative insights, with rADC serving as a complementary metric. Crucially, the combined diagnostic nomogram demonstrated robust diagnostic performance despite internal penalization. Pending prospective external validation, this tool may inform individualized diagnosis and optimize surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Single-view echocardiography-based deep learning for pulmonary hypertension detection: a multi-level supervised and explainable approach.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early identification of pulmonary hypertension (PH), particularly mild disease, remains challenging. We aimed to develop and validate a deep learning (DL) model for noninvasive PH screening using single-view transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), without reliance on Doppler measurements. METHODS: In this retrospective study, apical four-chamber (A4C) TTE cine loops were collected between January 2023 and June 2025. A total of 144 patients with PH confirmed by right heart catheterization (RHC), 17 RHC-confirmed non-PH patients, and 95 non-PH controls defined by TTE under strict inclusion criteria were included. An additional temporally independent validation cohort of 40 RHC-confirmed subjects was enrolled between December 2025 and May 2026. Multiple DL architectures were evaluated for detecting PH. Model performance was assessed at both sample and patient levels using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. RESULTS: A total of 256 patients with 318 TTE examinations were included for model development and independent validation, and an additional 40 RHC-confirmed subjects with 40 TTE examinations were included for temporal validation. The multi-level supervised model achieved the best performance among the evaluated architectures, with a patient-level AUROC of 1.000 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.998-1.000], sensitivity of 0.954, and specificity of 1.000 in the independent validation cohort. In the temporal validation cohort, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.843-0.992), with sensitivity of 0.875, specificity of 0.813, and accuracy of 0.850. In an analysis of 50 RHC-confirmed subjects, the DL model achieved an AUROC of 0.937 (95% CI: 0.865-0.987) for distinguishing mild PH from non-PH, with sensitivity of 0.857 and specificity of 0.864, compared with AUROCs of 0.607-0.825 for conventional echocardiographic parameters. CONCLUSIONS: We developed an interpretable DL framework based on single-view A4C echocardiography for noninvasive PH assessment. The model showed promising performance, including preserved sensitivity for mild PH. Further multicenter prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Impact of hypertriglyceridemia on right ventricular deformation in patients with left ventricular myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a significant risk factor for myocardial infarction (MI), adversely affecting left ventricular (LV) structure and function and worsening clinical outcomes. Given the interaction between ventricles, the right heart may also be affected by MI. This study investigated the additional effects of HTG on right ventricular (RV) deformation in patients with acute MI. METHODS: The study included 101 patients with MI [58 without HTG (HTG-) and 43 with HTG (HTG+)] and 83 control participants, all of whom underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. The patients with MI were categorized into HTG+ and HTG- subgroups. RV and LV function and strain were assessed, and multivariate linear regression was performed to identify determinants of RV peak strain (PS). RESULTS: Compared with the HTG- group, the HTG+ group exhibited higher total cholesterol and troponin levels (P=0.002 and P=0.043, respectively), as well as significantly lower RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05 after Bonferroni correction). RV radial PS was inversely correlated with LV mass (r=-0.349, P=0.021), total cholesterol (r=-0.402, P=0.007), troponin (r=-0.584, P<0.001), and infarct size (r=-0.410, P=0.006). RV circumferential PS was correlated with multiple LV parameters, lipids, and infarct extent (r=0.323 to 0.574; all P<0.05). After adjusting for age, sex, and blood pressure, HTG remained independently associated with impaired RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: HTG is associated with greater RV strain impairment in patients with MI. Our findings suggest that triglyceride levels and LV infarct extent may be associated with RV strain impairment, warranting further investigation in prospective studies.

articles.title: The added value of contrast-enhanced ultrasonography to BI-RADS in the evaluation of breast lesions presenting with pathological nipple discharge.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological nipple discharge (PND) is a frequent presentation in breast clinics, yet its accurate differentiation between benign and malignant lesions remains difficult due to the inherent limitations of current imaging tools. There is still a lack of a practical, non‑invasive approach that incorporates contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) features with the conventional Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) to improve the diagnostic yield. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and diagnostic performance of a rerated BI-RADS system combining ultrasound (US) and CEUS versus US BI-RADS alone for breast lesions causing PND. METHODS: A total of 217 consecutive patients with PND underwent conventional US and CEUS between January 2009 and August 2025. Each lesion was evaluated with US BI-RADS categories, then CEUS BI-RADS categories were re-rated based on US BI-RADS categories and CEUS scores. All responsible lesions were confirmed by pathological results through surgery or biopsy. To account for the potential correlation among multiple lesions from the same patient, we used generalized estimating equations with an exchangeable correlation structure for multivariate analysis to identify independent risk factors. The diagnostic performance of US BI-RADS and CEUS BI-RADS was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. RESULTS: There were 258 breast lesions from 217 patients consecutively evaluated in this retrospective study. A total of 57 lesions were pathologically confirmed to be malignant, and 201 were confirmed to be benign. There was a statistically significant difference in multiple clinical and ultrasonic features between malignant and benign lesions (P<0.05). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis based on generalized estimating equations identified age, size, enhancement range, enhancement order and spiculate sign as independent predictors of malignant breast lesions with discharge (all P<0.02). The BI-RADS categories based on CEUS showed higher sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV) and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) compared to US BI-RADS, which were 0.930 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.822-0.977], 0.945 (95% CI: 0.858-0.982) and 0.637 (95% CI: 0.575-0.695), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, CEUS BI-RADS demonstrates high sensitivity and NPV in evaluating breast lesions associated with PND. Although its overall discriminatory ability, as measured by AUROC, was not significantly different from that of conventional US BI-RADS when BI-RADS 4a lesions were considered test-positive, CEUS provides complementary functional information that aids in risk stratification. These findings position CEUS as a valuable adjunct to conventional US, particularly in refining the assessment of low-suspicion lesions and guiding biopsy decisions in patients with PND.

articles.title: Association between microwave ablation and remission in patients with Graves' hyperthyroidism receiving continuous antithyroid drug treatment: a single-arm prospective study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Graves' disease (GD) is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism. Nearly half of patients develop persistent/recurrent GD (prGD) after antithyroid drug (ATD) therapy. Microwave ablation (MWA) is a precise minimally invasive therapeutic modality; however, evidence regarding its efficacy for prGD remains limited. This study therefore evaluated the efficacy of MWA in treating prGD and investigated factors predictive of post-MWA remission. METHODS: This single-arm prospective study enrolled 45 patients with prGD who underwent bilateral thyroid MWA under ultrasound guidance at the Affiliated Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine between January 2023 and April 2024. The primary outcome was the remission rate during follow-up, defined as maintenance of normal thyroid function for at least 6 months after ATD discontinuation. Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test was used to analyze remission, and logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to identify factors associated with remission. RESULTS: The cohort included 34 females and 11 males, with a median follow-up of 31.00 (28.00, 33.00) months. Notable findings included a significant reduction in the median thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) receptor antibody level at the last follow-up (P<0.001). Both thyroid volume and the average methimazole (MMI) dose were significantly reduced (both P<0.001). At the last follow-up, remission was achieved in 29 patients, yielding a total remission rate of 64.44%. Patients in the remission group had smaller baseline thyroid volumes than those in the non-remission group. Preoperative thyroid volume was independently associated with remission [odds ratio (OR) =0.829; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.707-0.971; P=0.020], with an optimal cutoff of 29.35 mL [area under the curve (AUC) =74.4%; 95% CI: 0.596-0.892; sensitivity =72.4%; specificity =68.7%]. All nine patients with thyroid volumes less than 20 mL achieved remission. No severe complications were reported during the follow-up period. CONCLUSIONS: MWA was associated with decreased thyroid volume and reduced MMI dosage in patients with prGD, and clinical remission was observed in a subset of these patients. A preoperative thyroid volume of less than 29.35 mL is associated with a higher likelihood of remission.

articles.title: Combined non-contrast enhancement 3D bright-blood and 2D black-blood coronary magnetic resonance angiography for the assessment of coronary artery stenosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-contrast coronary magnetic resonance angiography (CMRA) offers a radiation- and contrast-free alternative for evaluating coronary artery disease, yet its clinical adoption has been constrained by suboptimal specificity, primarily due to flow-related artifacts and signal loss inherent to bright-blood imaging. Black-blood vessel wall imaging, by suppressing intraluminal blood signal, enables direct visualization of the coronary wall and may complement bright-blood CMRA to improve diagnostic accuracy. However, the additive value of a targeted sequential protocol combining these two techniques remains to be established. The objective of this study was to evaluate whether a sequential protocol combining three-dimensional (3D) bright-blood CMRA with lesion-directed two-dimensional (2D) black-blood coronary magnetic resonance (CMR) improves the diagnostic performance of non-contrast CMRA for detecting coronary artery stenosis, using computed tomography angiography as the reference standard. METHODS: From January 2025 to April 2025, consecutive patients with suspected coronary artery disease who were scheduled for dual-source computed tomography angiography and consented to undergo 3.0-T non-contrast CMRA were enrolled. The imaging protocol comprised free-breathing 3D bright-blood whole-heart CMRA, followed by lesion-directed 2D black-blood CMRA performed exclusively in segments with equivocal or suspicious findings on bright-blood imaging. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) served as the primary reference standard, with ICA performed in a subset of nine patients. Diagnostic performance for detecting significant (>50% diameter stenosis) and mild (25-49%) stenosis was assessed on a per-segment basis. Comparative analyses between bright-blood CMRA alone and the combined approach were performed using the McNemar test for paired proportions and DeLong's method for receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. RESULTS: A total of 114 vessel segments from 104 patients (mean age 63±13 years; 63 men)were included in the final analysis. The combination of bright-blood CMRA and 2D black-blood CMR demonstrated superior diagnostic performance compared with bright-blood CMRA alone for identifying significant stenosis (>50% diameter stenosis). Sensitivity was 97.9% [95% confidence interval (CI), 88.9-99.9%] versus 87.5% (95% CI, 72.3-93.9%; P=0.031), specificity was 98.5% (95% CI, 91.8-100.0%) versus 68.1% (95% CI, 52.4-76.5%; P<0.001), accuracy was 98.2% (95% CI, 93.8-99.8%) versus 76.3% (95% CI, 64.6-81.5%; P<0.001), and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.98 (95% CI, 95.2-99.1%) versus 0.75 (95% CI, 66.2-82.1%; P<0.001). In addition, the combined approach correctly identified non-significant stenosis (25-49% diameter stenosis) in 32 of 35 segments and significantly improved sensitivity [91.4% (95% CI, 76.8-98.0%) vs. 71.4% (95% CI, 53.7-85.4%); P=0.039]. CONCLUSIONS: The combination of 3D bright-blood CMRA and 2D black-blood CMR significantly enhances the diagnostic performance of non-contrast CMRA for detecting both significant and mild coronary artery stenosis.

articles.title: Apparent diffusion coefficient histogram parameters of the whole tumor based on whole-body magnetic resonance imaging can better characterize the tumor burden of multiple myeloma and predict survival prognosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) is characterized by a spatially heterogeneous tumor burden. Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI)-derived apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) histogram analysis may enable comprehensive characterization of tumor burden. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of using whole-tumor ADC histogram parameters based on WB-MRI images to assess tumor burden and evaluate their prognostic value in NDMM patients. METHODS: There were 95 NDMM patients categorized into focal lesion and whole-tumor groups in this retrospective study. Correlation analysis of ADC histogram parameters with clinical parameters was performed in the two groups respectively. In the survival analysis section, 64 patients were included, Cox regression analysis was used to conduct univariate and multivariate analysis of potential risk factors for overall survival (OS). X-tile plots were used to determine the optimal cutoffs based on the highest χ2 value defined by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and log-rank test. RESULTS: Apart from ADCmax, there was statistically significant difference in the remaining ADC histogram parameters between two groups (all P<0.05). In the whole-tumor group, ADCmean (r=0.434, P<0.01), ADC5th (r=0.334, P<0.01), ADC10th (r=0.371, P<0.01), ADC25th (r=0.416, P<0.01), ADC50th (r=0.431, P<0.01), ADC75th (r=0.424, P<0.01), ADC90th (r=0.398, P<0.01), and ADC95th (r=0.402, P<0.01) were positively correlated with bone marrow plasma cell (BMPC). Multivariate Cox regression showed that BMPC (P=0.022), β2-MG (P=0.016), ADC25th (P=0.023), ADC95th (P<0.001) and entropy (P=0.001) were all independent prognostic factors for poor OS. X-tile plots and the Kaplan-Meier survival curves showed that BMPC (>70%), β2-MG (>10.68 mg/L), ADC25th (>0.37 mm2/s), ADC95th (>1.03 mm2/s) and low entropy (≤3.56) achieved worse prognosis. CONCLUSIONS: Whole tumor histogram parameters can better characterize the tumor burden of multiple myeloma (MM) patients than those of the focal lesion groups. The Cox regression risk model based on the whole tumor ADC (wtADC) histogram parameters and clinical parameters can predict the survival status.

articles.title: Salivary gland dynamic imaging combined with tomosynthesis fusion imaging for evaluating postoperative salivary gland function changes in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer undergoing initial 131I therapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: 131I therapy is a targeted therapy for patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) after surgery, reducing the risk of tumor recurrence and metastasis. Radioactive iodine can accumulate in the salivary glands, causing radiation damage. Dynamic imaging of the salivary glands can objectively assess the morphology and function of the salivary glands, making it a simple and non-invasive diagnostic method. The purpose of this study was to quantitatively analyze salivary gland function changes in patients with DTC undergoing postoperative 131I therapy using salivary gland dynamic imaging combined with tomographic fusion imaging. METHODS: A retrospective study enrolled 49 patients with DTC who underwent total thyroidectomy and received initial 131I therapy (dose: 5.55 GBq) between May 2020 and March 2024. Salivary gland dynamic imaging was performed on the day before 131I therapy and at least 4 months post-therapy. Salivary gland dynamic imaging was performed to measure the concentration index (CI), secretion index (SI), maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of bilateral salivary glands, as well as SUVmax in the temporal region. The CI, SI, and the relative SUVmax (rSUVmax) in bilateral salivary glands to the temporal region were used as evaluation indicators. RESULTS: There were no statistically significant differences in the CI or SI of bilateral salivary glands before and after 131I therapy (P>0.05). The rSUVmax of parotid gland to temporal region showed a statistically significant difference before and after 131I therapy (P<0.05), whereas the rSUVmax of submandibular gland to temporal region showed no statistically significant difference (P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DTC undergoing postoperative treatment, administering 131I therapy at an initial dose of 5.55 GBq with acid stimulation in the early phase can impair parotid gland function. Quantitative analysis using salivary gland dynamic imaging combined with tomographic fusion imaging enables accurate assessment of salivary gland function.

articles.title: Determining malignancy in thyroid nodules featuring anterior macrocalcifications with strong posterior acoustic shadowing: the combined utility of US-FNA and BRAF V600E mutation analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Thyroid nodules with anterior macrocalcifications and strong posterior acoustic shadowing present diagnostic challenges due to uncertain malignancy risk. The diagnostic value of combining ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration (US-FNA) with BRAF V600E mutation analysis in these nodules remains inadequately evaluated. This study aimed to determine the malignancy risk in such nodules and assess the efficacy of the combined diagnostic approach. METHODS: A retrospective study of 79 thyroid nodules exhibiting macrocalcifications at the anterior margin with strong posterior acoustic shadowing was performed. Based on sonographic features, we classified hyperechoic macrocalcifications into four subtypes: Type I (smooth arc-shaped eggshell-like), Type II (discontinuous arc-shaped, irregularly thickened), Type III (multiple macrocalcifications arranged as layers), and Type IV (multiple macrocalcifications stacked or clustered together). According to BRAF V600E mutation or surgical pathology results, the study determined the malignant risk for anteriorly macrocalcified nodules and assessed the diagnostic efficacy of both US-FNA and BRAF V600E mutation testing. RESULTS: The proportion of Type II macrocalcification was relatively high (70.0%) in the BRAF V600E mutation-positive cases. The malignant rate was 34.6% (18/52) for anteriorly macrocalcified nodules on US-FNA cytology and 25.3% (20/79) via BRAF V600E mutation testing. US-FNA yielded inconclusive results in 31.6% (25/79) of cases, predominantly 84.0% (21/25) with Type I/II macrocalcifications. The combination of US-FNA and BRAF V600E testing yielded a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 75.0%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 94.7%, negative predictive value (NPV) of 100%, and diagnostic accuracy of 95.4%, compared to US-FNA alone (94.4%, 75.0%, 94.4%, 75.0%, and 90.9%, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Thyroid nodules featuring anterior macrocalcifications with strong posterior acoustic shadowing carry a significant moderate risk, and Type II calcification serves as a key imaging biomarker for malignancy. Combining US-FNA with BRAF V600E testing can enhance the diagnostic accuracy for thyroid nodules with anterior macrocalcifications.

articles.title: Interobserver agreement of non-parallel transmission technology zoomed-diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for ordinal biparametric Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS)-based scoring in bladder cancer lesions ≥1 cm.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preoperative assessment of muscle invasion in bladder cancer using the Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) relies heavily on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), but conventional single-shot echo-planar imaging diffusion-weighted imaging (ss-EPI-DWI) may be limited by image distortion and artifacts, potentially affecting interobserver agreement. Zoomed diffusion-weighted imaging without parallel transmission technology (non-pTx zoomed-DWI) may improve image quality. This study aimed to compare the interobserver agreement of non-pTx zoomed-DWI versus conventional ss-EPI-DWI for ordinal biparametric VI-RADS-based scoring in bladder cancer lesions ≥1 cm across different morphological types among radiologists with varying levels of experience. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included patients with pathologically confirmed bladder cancer who underwent preoperative biparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), including T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), conventional ss-EPI-DWI, and non-pTx zoomed-DWI, before transurethral resection of bladder tumor or radical cystectomy. Three radiologists independently assigned ordinal biparametric VI-RADS-based F-scores from 1 to 5 for each eligible lesion using ss-EPI-DWI and non-pTx zoomed-DWI datasets separately. T2WI was used for lesion localization and morphological classification, whereas the corresponding DWI sequence, including high-b-value DWI images and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, was used to assign ordinal biparametric VI-RADS-based F-scores according to the standard VI-RADS scoring criteria. Subjective image quality was rated on a 4-point scale. Interobserver agreement was assessed using linear weighted kappa statistics with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: A total of 162 patients (138 males, 24 females; median age 67 years) with 214 eligible bladder cancer lesions were included. Non-pTx zoomed-DWI provided significantly higher subjective image quality scores than ss-EPI-DWI for both readers (P<0.001). Based on the original ordinal VI-RADS-based F-scores, overall pairwise interobserver agreement was good with ss-EPI-DWI (linear weighted κ=0.708-0.761) and excellent with non-pTx zoomed-DWI (linear weighted κ=0.851-0.870). In morphology-specific analyses, agreement also improved with non-pTx zoomed-DWI across lesion subgroups. The improvement was particularly evident in broad-based nodules, for which agreement increased from good with ss-EPI-DWI (κ=0.700-0.752) to excellent with non-pTx zoomed-DWI (κ=0.892-0.919), and in nodules with pedicles, for which agreement improved from moderate-to-good (κ=0.535-0.640) to good-to-excellent (κ=0.786-0.847). CONCLUSIONS: Non-pTx zoomed-DWI improved subjective image quality and interobserver agreement for ordinal biparametric VI-RADS-based scoring in bladder cancer lesions ≥1 cm compared with conventional ss-EPI-DWI. These findings suggest that non-pTx zoomed-DWI may support more consistent MRI-based assessment of muscle invasion risk, particularly in morphologically complex lesions. Further prospective studies with lesion-level pathological correlation are needed to determine whether improved agreement translates into improved diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Contrastive adversarial mix-up learning for unsupervised cross-modality image segmentation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) has been extensively investigated in terms of its ability to address the performance degradation caused by distribution shifts between labeled source-domain images and unlabeled target-domain images. In radiotherapy, this problem is particularly relevant for the transfer of segmentation knowledge from planning computed tomography (CT) to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), for which target-domain annotations are limited. This study aimed to develop a contrastive adversarial mix-up learning framework for unsupervised cross-modality image segmentation. METHODS: A UDA framework integrating mix-up augmentation (MA) and contrastive adversarial learning (AL) was developed. This framework included a shared-weight redistribution network to reduce cross-domain appearance discrepancies, a mix-up consistency strategy to constrain segmentation predictions of mixed-domain images, and contrastive AL to regulate the relationship between redistributed mixture images and mixed redistributed images. The method was evaluated with two in-house CT-CBCT datasets comprising 112 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and 112 patients with breast cancer, with 12 patients from each dataset randomly selected for testing. Generalizability was further evaluated in 75 patients from the public Brain Tumor Segmentation 2018 (BraTS2018) dataset, with 80% used for training and 20% for testing. Segmentation performance was assessed via the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff distance (HD), and Jaccard index. RESULTS: On the in-house CT-CBCT datasets, the complete UDA + MA + AL framework achieved DSC values of 82.08%, 85.81%, 78.60%, and 60.75% for the breast cancer clinical target volume (CTV), heart, head-and-neck cancer CTV, and parotid glands, respectively; meanwhile, compared with the UDA-only framework, the corresponding absolute DSC improvements of the complete framework were 8.70, 1.02, 3.28, and 3.04 percentage points, respectively. On the BraTS2018 dataset, the proposed framework achieved DSC values of 63.56%, 67.81%, 85.47%, and 74.16% for tasks adapting T2-weighted magnetic resonance image (T2) to T1-weighted magnetic resonance image (T1), T2 to T1 contrast enhanced, T2 to fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), and FLAIR to T2, respectively. Overall, the proposed method achieved an average DSC improvement of 3.53 percentage points compared with representative UDA-based segmentation methods. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed contrastive adversarial mix-up learning framework improved unsupervised cross-modality segmentation performance across CT-CBCT and multisequence magnetic resonance imaging adaptation tasks. By combining cross-domain redistribution, mix-up consistency learning, and contrastive AL, the framework can provide enhanced robustness for variations in image appearance and anatomical structure while maintaining segmentation consistency.

articles.title: Left ventricular function and volumes from cardiac magnetic resonance and gated [13N]-ammonia positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with ischemia with no obstructive coronary arteries: a prospective head-to-head comparison using hybrid positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) has been widely validated for the assessment of left ventricular (LV) volumes and function. This study aimed to compare the accuracy of LV volumes and functional parameters derived from 13N-ammonia PET with those obtained by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using CMR as the reference standard. METHODS: A total of 75 consecutive patients with known or suspected ischemia with no obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) who simultaneously underwent ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET and CMR using a hybrid PET/magnetic resonance (MR) scanner were enrolled in this prospective study. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), left ventricular end-systolic volume (LVESV), left ventricular stroke volume (LVSV), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and regional wall motion score (RWMS) were derived from both imaging modalities and compared using correlation and Bland-Altman (BA) analyses. Additionally, inter- and intraobserver variability in LV volumetric parameters and LVEF were evaluated for both imaging modalities. RESULTS: The correlation between PET and CMR was strong for LV volumes (r>0.83) and moderate for LVEF (r=0.65). The moderate LVEF correlation may be partially explained by the narrow range of LVEF values across the study cohort. Moreover, the agreement between 13N-ammonia PET and CMR for LVEF was good, with minimal bias (-0.57%); however, 13N-ammonia PET systematically underestimated LV volumes, with negative biases for LVEDV (-7.76 mL), LVESV (-3.28 mL), and LVSV (-5.33 mL). Similar, strong correlations and good agreement were observed in patients with reduced myocardial flow reserve (MFR). For both PET and CMR, inter- and intraobserver agreement for LV volumes and LVEF was high and comparable between the two modalities. In addition, RWMSs derived from ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET and CMR also exhibited good agreement (kappa =0.84±0.02). CONCLUSIONS: LVEF and RWMS can be reliably and accurately quantified by ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET, although LV volumes are systematically underestimated compared with those quantified by CMR. ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET may serve as a complementary modality for the assessment of LV systolic function; however, CMR remains the benchmark for LV volumetric measurement and myocardial tissue assessment.

articles.title: Evaluation of Delphi high-resolution computed tomography phenotype classification for treatment-naïve patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The recently developed Delphi consensus provides a simplified high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) phenotype classification system for pulmonary sarcoidosis. This study aimed to investigate the clinical value of HRCT phenotype classification from the Delphi consensus study on pulmonary sarcoidosis in treatment‑naïve patients and to identify potential refinements for classifying early‑stage sarcoidosis. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 278 treatment‑naïve patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis. HRCT signs were scored, and clinical data were recorded for all patients. Patients were followed up to observe the treatment effect, recurrence, and onset of pulmonary fibrosis. Associations between HRCT findings, pulmonary function tests (PFTs), early corticosteroid response, recurrence, and fibrosis progression were analyzed. The imaging data were then classified into seven Delphi-defined HRCT phenotypes to evaluate their clinical and prognostic relevance. RESULTS: HRCT signs, including nodules, consolidation, and ground-glass opacity (GGO), were significantly associated with decreased PFT parameters. The presence of central consolidation and nodules was predictive of a favorable early treatment response, while the presence of coarse granular GGOs was associated with a significantly higher risk of recurrence. In terms of Delphi HRCT phenotype, there were 196 patients with the nonfibrotic phenotype (70.5%) and 28 patients with likely-to-be fibrotic phenotypes (10.1%) in our cohort. However, there were unclassifiable cases, including those with isolated lymphadenopathy (12.2%), GGO (5.4%), and pleural effusion‑dominant (1.8%) patterns. Likely-to-be fibrotic phenotypes were associated with the greatest impairment of pulmonary function and the highest risk of fibrosis. The consolidation-dominant type was also associated with an increased risk of fibrosis. According to Cox proportional hazards regression, the isolated lymphadenopathy type was associated with a lower risk of recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: The Delphi HRCT phenotype classification is clinically useful but may not be sufficient to fully characterize early-stage pulmonary sarcoidosis. The isolated lymphadenopathy and GGO-dominant types should be considered in the future framework due to their distinct functional and prognostic relevance.

articles.title: Incremental prognostic value of hepatic tissue alterations derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy: a case-control study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic injury occurs in patients with cardiovascular disease and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. The prognostic value of hepatic tissue alterations in patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the incremental prognostic value of hepatic native T1 in predicting sustained ventricular arrhythmia (VA) in patients with ARVC. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with definite ARVC who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) examinations between August 2014 and October 2024. Hepatic native T1 values were derived from standard cardiac T1 maps. The clinical outcome was the first occurrence of sustained VA. Cox regression analysis was used to determine the association of variables with sustained VA. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated according to the concordance statistic (C-statistic), likelihood ratio test, and the continuous net reclassification index. RESULTS: A total of 94 patients with definite ARVC (mean age 37.3±14.2 years; 67% male) were included. At a median follow-up of 39 months, sustained VA occurred in 34 (36%) patients. In multivariable Cox analysis, hepatic native T1 was an independent predictor of sustained VA [hazard ratio (HR) =1.02, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.00-1.03; P=0.025]. A model combining hepatic native T1 with the ARVC risk score and CMR-derived right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RV GLS) showed improved discrimination and calibration for sustained VA (C-statistic =0.760; likelihood ratio =20.14) compared with models composed of ARVC risk score alone (C-statistic =0.680; likelihood ratio =9.20; P<0.001) or the ARVC risk score and RV GLS (C-statistic =0.735; likelihood ratio =15.30; P=0.028). CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic native T1 derived from cardiac T1 maps was an independent predictor of sustained VA in patients with ARVC, providing incremental prognostic value when incorporated into a model with ARVC risk score and RV GLS.

articles.title: Ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics with explainable machine learning for predicting benign and malignant thyroid nodules in lymphocytic thyroiditis: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Thyroid nodules (TNs) with lymphocytic thyroiditis (LT) complicate ultrasound (US) assessment, and few prediction models have been validated in this population. The aim of this study is to develop and validate a US-based deep learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) model for predicting malignancy in TNs coexisting with LT. METHODS: This multicenter hybrid study enrolled 640 patients with pathologically confirmed TNs and concomitant LT. The cohort comprised a training set from Anhui Medical University First Affiliated Hospital (Jixi Road Campus), Anhui Medical University First Affiliated Hospital (High-tech Campus), and Affiliated Hospital of Integration Chinese and Western Medicine with Nanjing University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (retrospective, n=411), an external test set from Yijishan Hospital of Wannan Medical College (retrospective, n=162), and a validation set (prospective, n=67). Deep learning (DL) and handcrafted radiomics features were extracted separately from US images. After feature fusion, the features were Z-score normalized and selected using the Mann-Whitney U test or Chi-squared test, with Fisher's exact test used when appropriate, followed by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. A DL radiomics (DLR) model was developed based on 10 machine learning algorithms and subsequently incorporated with independent clinical factors through logistic regression to build a DLRN. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration and decision curve, along with SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis for interpretability. RESULTS: Logistic regression was selected as the optimal DLR algorithm, achieving AUCs of 0.90 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.87-0.93] in the training set, 0.90 (95% CI: 0.84-0.94) in the external test set, and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.71-0.91) in the prospective validation set. The DLRN, refined by integrating independent clinical factors via logistic regression, demonstrated superior discrimination with AUCs of 0.93, 0.94, and 0.92 in the training, external test, and prospective validation sets, respectively. The DLRN model demonstrated robust clinical applicability, as evidenced by calibration and decision curve analyses. SHAP analysis enhanced DLRN interpretability by quantifying feature contributions to individual predictions and overall model output. CONCLUSIONS: The DLRN model was designed for the preoperative identification of malignant TNs in LT, thereby facilitating personalized treatment.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-based prostate cancer risk stratification via large-scale ultrasound images paired with histopathology.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer (PCa) is primarily screened and diagnosed via prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, digital rectal examination (DRE), multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), and transrectal ultrasound (TRUS). Nevertheless, an open research challenge remains to develop artificial intelligence (AI) tools that enable non-invasive, accurate diagnosis, and risk stratification of PCa. This study aimed to construct an Anatomy-Aware Transformer (AAT) model based on a large-scale dataset of paired TRUS images and corresponding histopathological findings, and to further validate the clinical value of TRUS-based AI for PCa diagnosis and risk stratification. METHODS: Sagittal TRUS images were prospectively acquired pre- and intra-biopsy. Based on the intra-biopsy images, the prostate contour and the location of biopsy tissue cores on pre-biopsy images were manually annotated. According to the characteristic features of the prostate and periprostatic tissues, we designed a feature screening module and a feature integration module, and further constructed an AAT model that deeply integrates prostate regional segmentation and PCa diagnosis tasks. The diagnostic performance of the AAT model in PCa detection and risk stratification was evaluated by comparing its results with those of 18 classic models and four ultrasonographers. RESULTS: A Primary Dataset (18,424 images; May 2022 to Dec 2023) supported training/internal validation, and an External Dataset (683 images; Jun to Jul 2024) external validation. The AAT model outperformed all comparison models across all tasks: PCa detection (internal accuracy 0.977 vs. 0.655-0.972; external accuracy 0.810 vs. 0.616-0.737), clinically significant PCa (CSPCa) detection (internal/external accuracy: 0.936/0.843 vs. 0.697-0.934/0.304-0.762), 3-category risk stratification (internal/external accuracy: 0.828/0.836 vs. 0.697-0.822/0.642-0.768), and 5-category stratification (internal/external accuracy: 0.760/0.722 vs. 0.655-0.760/0.690-0.715). AAT's PCa diagnostic accuracy (0.943) exceeded ultrasonographers (0.567-0.757) and improved their performance by 0.036-0.304 as an aid. CONCLUSIONS: We developed a novel AAT model that exhibits outstanding performance in diagnosing PCa and CSPCa, with reliable efficacy in PCa risk stratification. This non-invasive model effectively improves the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasonographers and enables individualized clinical management for PCa patients with varying risk levels, showing promising clinical translation potential.

articles.title: Two parallel systems constructed from complementary optical coherence tomography and histopathology for the assessment of murine intestinal inflammation: a dual-modality assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Quantitative assessment of intestinal inflammation among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains a clinical challenge. Conventional histopathology lacks robust quantification, and a real-time, noninvasive alternative is needed. This study aimed to establish a quantitative histopathological system for IBD and to develop a corresponding optical coherence tomography (OCT) system for real-time detection. METHODS: Murine models for both ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn disease (CD) were developed, and corresponding intestinal histopathological samples were obtained. Artificial intelligence-based image segmentation enabled systematic analysis of pathological images, including two-dimensional planar structures, three-dimensional volumetric morphology, texture features, and grayscale histograms, through which a comprehensive histopathological evaluation system for precise quantitative assessment of intestinal inflammation severity was established. Based on this framework, an OCT system was developed for intestinal wall structural analysis, which demonstrated high concordance with histopathological benchmarks while enabling real-time, noninvasive quantitative detection. RESULTS: Both systems effectively differentiated UC, CD, and normal tissue. Planar histopathology revealed significant differences in these models in comparison to controls. The median mucosal fold angle was markedly elevated in UC [median 63.854°, interquartile range (IQR), 37.110-91.151°] and CD (49.925°, IQR, 34.140-62.550°) mice as compared controls (7.635°, IQR, 5.975-10.873°) (both P values <0.001). Submucosal area and cell count were higher in both disease groups, while the gland count was lower (all P values <0.05). Mucosal area ratio decreased from 73.608% in controls to 66.703% in UC mice (P=0.020) and to 59.182% in CD mice (P<0.001), whereas the submucosa ratio increased from 8.127% to 10.812% (P=0.031) and 16.076% (P<0.001), respectively. Three-dimensional reconstruction confirmed increased intestinal wall volumes in both disease groups (all P values <0.05). OCT texture analysis showed decreased energy and increased entropy in the UC and CD groups as compared to the control group (P<0.05), indicating disrupted microstructure. Gray-scale analysis revealed a shift toward lower values in diseased tissues (P<0.001). Pathological texture analysis demonstrated significantly elevated contrast in CD mice (median 153.425) as compared with UC (62.160) and control (70.495) mice (P<0.001), suggesting that CD and UC each have distinct textural signatures. CONCLUSIONS: This work establishes an integrated framework: a quantitative histopathological system providing novel diagnostic indices, and a complementary OCT system enabling real-time assessment. It offers a proof of concept for multimodal quantitative biomarkers in IBD, an objective tool for preclinical research, and a foundation for future OCT endoscopic applications in clinical evaluation.

articles.title: A collaborative hybrid network with aggregated attention for pulmonary nodule detection.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of early detection for improving patient survival. Current imaging‑based methods for pulmonary nodule (PN) detection are often limited by low efficiency and suboptimal accuracy, falling short of the demands for precise clinical diagnosis. The baseline YOLOv8 model, although efficient, is prone to missed detections due to non-maximum suppression (NMS)‑induced suppression of small nodules and insufficient feature extraction for morphologically complex lesions. To address these clinical challenges, this study aimed to optimize YOLOv8 by integrating a real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR) decoder head and an aggregated attention mechanism, thereby improving detection sensitivity and accuracy for PNs of varying sizes and shapes. METHODS: The proposed model, termed YOLOv8‑RTA, integrates an RT‑DETR‑based transformer decoder head into YOLOv8, replacing the original detection head to mitigate NMS‑induced suppression of true boxes, and introduces an aggregated attention mechanism within the backbone to expand the effective receptive field and enhance deep feature discriminability. Training and evaluation were performed on the Tianchi dataset, with five‑fold cross‑validation and an external test on 50 hospital Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) computed tomography (CT) scans. RESULTS: YOLOv8‑RTA achieved precision of 93.28%, recall of 92.4%, and mean average precision at 50% intersection over union (mAP50) of 94.98% on the Tianchi dataset. Compared to the baseline YOLOv8 model, which achieved an mAP50 of 90.6%, the proposed method improved the detection accuracy by 4.38 percentage points. It also outperformed RT‑DETR‑R18, which attained an mAP50 of 93.51%, by a margin of 1.47 percentage points. The model contains only 6.24 million parameters and runs at 12.2 giga floating point operations per second (GFLOPs). In five‑fold cross‑validation, the mAP50 ranged from 75.4% to 99.3%, with a mean value of 91.5%. On the external PACS dataset, the model detected all 50 nodules, achieving a mean confidence score of 0.86 for nodules smaller than 5 mm. CONCLUSIONS: This study proposes YOLOv8‑RTA, a collaborative hybrid network that combines an RT‑DETR decoder head and an aggregated attention module to enhance multi‑scale feature extraction and discriminative representation for PN detection. On the Tianchi dataset, the model achieved improved performance over baseline YOLOv8 and RT‑DETR‑R18, with gains of 4.38 and 1.47 percentage points in mAP50, respectively, while maintaining a lightweight architecture of only 6.24 million parameters. A preliminary test on 50 real‑world PACS CT images suggests potential clinical feasibility, with all nodules successfully detected in this limited cohort. These findings indicate that YOLOv8‑RTA offers a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade‑off for PN screening. Future work will focus on larger multi‑center validation, patient‑level cross‑validation, and extension to three-dimensional (3D) context modelling.

articles.title: A deep learning-based model combining quantitative parameters of initial chest computed tomography and clinical variables for the prediction of posttraumatic acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) frequently complicates severe trauma, and early risk stratification for this condition remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a combined prediction model integrating deep learning-based quantitative parameters of initial chest computed tomography (CT) with clinical variables for the early prediction of posttraumatic ARDS, with a focus on automation and interpretability for potential integration with emergency workflows. METHODS: A total of 173 patients with trauma admitted to West China Hospital of Sichuan University from January to June 2024 were retrospectively screened, and 105 patients were finally enrolled (34 in the ARDS group and 71 in the nonARDS group). Clinical data were collected, and quantitative parameters (e.g., opacity score, opacity volume, opacity percentage, highattenuation opacity volume, and mean CT value) were automatically extracted with deep learning-based CT quantitative analysis software. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with ARDS. The final multivariate model was expressed as follows: logit(ARDS risk) = -4.623 + [0.142 × Injury Severity Score (ISS)] + [0.247 × procalcitonin (PCT)] + (0.113 × bilateral lung opacity percentage). Model stability was evaluated via bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions), and the predictive performance was assessed according to the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. RESULTS: Compared with the non-ARDS group, the ARDS group had a higher ISS (40 vs. 25, P<0.001), lactate level (3.9 vs. 1.9 mmol/L, P<0.001), and PCT level (3.2 vs. 0.2 ng/mL, P<0.001), as well as a lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (12 vs. 15, P<0.001) and SpO2 (94.8% vs. 96.7%, P=0.038). The ARDS group also had a significantly higher bilateral lung opacity volume (186.3 vs. 56.7 mL, P=0.001), opacity percentage (5.2% vs. 1.8%, P=0.002), and high-attenuation opacity volume (45.8 vs. 9.0 mL, P=0.001). Multivariate analysis identified the independent predictors of ARDS to be ISS [odds ratio (OR) =1.15; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.06-1.24; P<0.001], PCT (OR =1.28; 95% CI: 1.04-1.58; P=0.02), and bilateral lung opacity percentage (OR =1.12; 95% CI: 1.04-1.21; P=0.004). The combined model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.892 (95% CI: 0.832-0.952). At the optimal cutoff of 0.385, the sensitivity and specificity were 82.4% and 85.9%, respectively. Bootstrap internal validation confirmed good model stability (mean AUC =0.878; 95% CI: 0.821-0.934). CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative parameters of initial chest CT within 24 hours after trauma, especially bilateral lung opacity percentage, are associated with the development of ARDS in patients with trauma and may serve as objective imaging biomarkers for early risk assessment. The prediction model combining ISS score and PCT with automated CT quantitative parameters demonstrated good discriminative ability (AUC =0.892) and clinical operability and can be automated within minutes in a research setting. Further implementation studies are needed before the model can be implemented after the initial CT scan in clinical settings; nonetheless, the model may serve as a decision support tool and as a component in implementing early lung-protective strategies.

articles.title: Utilization of 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT improves the gross tumor volume delineation in nasopharyngeal carcinoma within a safe radiation dose to organs at risk.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate delineation of the nasopharynx gross tumor volume (GTVnx) of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is crucial for patients requiring radiotherapy, as it correlates with prognosis. Current GTVnx delineation methods have significant shortcomings, often resulting in insufficient coverage of the radiotherapy target area. Gallium-68-labeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (68Ga-FAPI) is an emerging and promising tumor imaging agent. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of combining 68Ga-FAPI positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) for delineating GTVnx in NPC. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 19 patients with NPC who underwent 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT from August 2022 to August 2023. GTVnx were delineated, quantified, and compared based on enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT, and the fusion of both imaging modalities, and were respectively named and abbreviated as GTVnx-MRI, GTVnx-FAPI, and GTVnx-MRI + FAPI. GTVnx-FAPI was automatically delineated using maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) thresholds, with the optimal threshold determined by the Jaccard index and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Radiotherapy plans were developed based on GTVnx-MRI and GTVnx-MRI + FAPI to assess radiation doses to organs at risk (OARs). A paired t-test was employed to compare variables among groups. RESULTS: Nineteen pathologically confirmed NPC patients [mean age, 48.84±12.12 years (range, 24-70 years); 12 men (63.16%)] were enrolled. All included NPC patients demonstrated high 68Ga-FAPI uptake in their primary tumor lesions. The 20% SUVmax on 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT of the primary tumor (GTVnx-FAPI20%) was determined to be the most suitable threshold for guiding GTVnx-FAPI with an ICC of 0.891. The GTVnx-MRI + FAPI20% was significant lager than both GTVnx-MRI and GTVnx-FAPI20%, with average measurements of 24.92±17.31, 17.44±13.12, and 16.29±11.15 cm3, respectively (P<0.001). In the radiotherapy plan based on GTVnx-MRI + FAPI20%, radiation dose to all OARs was not increased significantly compared to that based on GTVnx-MRI. CONCLUSIONS: The combined use of 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT shows potential to enhance the delineation of GTVnx in NPC patients while maintaining OAR doses within acceptable limits.

articles.title: CT-guided hybrid cryo-thermal co-ablation versus microwave ablation for stage I renal cell carcinoma: a real-world propensity score-matched comparative study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive ablation is an established treatment for stage I renal cell carcinoma (RCC), but comparative evidence is limited. This study presents an exploratory feasibility comparison of co-ablation (Co-A), a hybrid cryo-thermal technique combining liquid-nitrogen freezing with ethanol-mediated heating, with microwave ablation (MWA) in perioperative safety, renal function preservation, and short-term oncologic outcomes. METHODS: Consecutive patients with clinical RCC who underwent computed tomography (CT)-guided percutaneous ablation from January 2017 to December 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Treatment selection reflected routine clinical judgment. This retrospective study was designed as an exploratory analysis. Propensity score matching (1:2) was performed using age, sex, baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), tumor size, and RENAL nephrometry score (Radius, Exophytic/endophytic properties, Nearness to collecting system, Anterior/posterior, and Location relative to polar lines). RESULTS: Among 102 screened patients, 78 met eligibility criteria before matching. After matching, 45 patients were included: 15 treated with Co-A and 30 with MWA. All Co-A procedures were completed under local anesthesia, whereas 9 MWA procedures required general anesthesia (P=0.012). Co-A had longer procedure duration (86.2±22.0 vs. 45.4±11.9 min; P<0.001) but shorter hospital stay (2.9±1.4 vs. 4.5±2.6 days; P=0.021). Notably, the shorter hospital stay in the Co-A group should be interpreted with caution, as it may be confounded by the exclusive use of local anesthesia rather than the ablation modality itself. Minor bleeding was more frequent after Co-A (60.0% vs. 23.3%, P=0.039). Short-term eGFR decline was similar between groups (-5.6±11.1 vs. -7.4±11.5 mL/min/1.73 m2; P=0.65). During a median 24-month follow-up, local recurrence occurred in 2 Co-A and 1 MWA patient (13.3% vs. 3.3%; P=0.278). CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory feasibility study suggests that Co-A and MWA demonstrate similar short-term renal functional outcomes in patients with stage I RCC. Co-A was feasible under local anesthesia and associated with shorter hospitalization, but required longer procedure times and was associated with more minor bleeding events. Differences in hospital stay should be interpreted cautiously due to potential anesthesia-related confounding. Oncologic comparisons require cautious interpretation.

articles.title: Unipolar electrogram-guided vs. ablation index-guided high-power short-duration pulmonary vein isolation in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: a single-center randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is the cornerstone of catheter ablation for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF). The ablation index (AI) provides an estimate of lesion size and depth, but does not definitively confirm transmurality. Complete elimination of the negative component of the unipolar electrogram (UPE) has been proposed as a marker of transmural lesion formation. High-power short-duration (HPSD) radiofrequency ablation (RFA) produces more homogeneous lesions with clearer boundaries and thus may be more suitable for PVI. This study aimed to assess the AI values achieved during PVI using UPE-guided HPSD RFA and to compare the efficacy and safety of UPE-guided vs. fixed AI-guided HPSD RFA in patients with PAF. METHODS: A total of 276 patients with PAF were randomly assigned to two groups: the UPE group and the AI group. In the UPE group (n=136), the ablation endpoint for each lesion was defined as continuation of ablation for 2 seconds after conversion of the UPE morphology from RS to R. In the AI group (n=140), the ablation endpoint for each lesion was achievement of a predefined target AI value (400-450 for the anterior wall and 360-380 for the posterior wall). The pulmonary vein (PV) first-pass isolation rate, acute PV reconnection (APVR) rate, and atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence rate were compared between groups. RESULTS: The AI values were significantly lower in the UPE group than in the AI group (P<0.001). The inter-lesion distance (ILD) was significantly greater in the UPE group than in the AI group (P<0.001). The left and right PV first-pass isolation rates were higher in the UPE group (93.4% vs. 85.0%, P=0.03; and 95.6% vs. 89.3%, P=0.048, respectively). APVR occurred less frequently in the UPE group than in the AI group (11.0% vs. 20.0%, P=0.040). At 12 months post-procedure, AF recurrence was observed in 13 patients (9.6%) in the UPE group and 14 patients (10.0%) in the AI group (P=0.902). Three patients in the UPE group and four patients in the AI group developed inguinal hematoma (2.2% vs. 2.9%, P>0.99). CONCLUSIONS: Both UPE-guided and AI-guided HPSD RFA were effective and safe in patients with PAF. UPE-guided ablation was associated with lower AI values, higher PV first-pass isolation rates, and a lower incidence of APVR. These findings suggest that UPE-guided HPSD RFA may provide a more individualized approach to PVI than fixed AI-guided ablation alone.

articles.title: Vessel wall MRI predictors of postprocedural new ischemic brain lesions after endovascular treatment for basilar artery stenosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)-detected new ischemic brain lesions (NIBL) are common complications after endovascular treatment (EVT) for basilar artery stenosis (BAS), directly impacting functional outcomes in patients. This study aimed to explore the association between vulnerable plaque markers identified by high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (HR-MRI) and NIBL, and to clarify their predictive value for postprocedural ischemic events. METHODS: A total of 373 patients with BAS who underwent EVT were retrospectively enrolled in this study. Patients were classified into DWI-positive (DWI+) and DWI-negative (DWI-) groups based on the presence of NIBL on DWI within 48 hours post-procedurally. Plaque burden, distribution, remodeling type, enhancement rate, and degree of stenosis were evaluated using HR-MRI. To determine independent predictors of NIBL post-procedurally, multivariable logistic regression was applied. RESULTS: NIBL developed in 188 patients (50.4%), with a mean age of 61.76±7.83 years, including 84 males. The DWI+ group exhibited significantly higher rates of positive remodeling (PR) (51.1% vs. 37.8%, P=0.01) and plaque enhancement (PE) (87.2% vs. 75.7%, P=0.004), as well as a greater plaque burden (13.38±40.75 vs. 6.06±29.77, P=0.033), compared to the DWI- group. Multivariate logistic regression identified PE [odds ratio (OR) =2.09, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18-3.70, P=0.011] and PR (OR =1.77, 95% CI: 1.03-3.06, P=0.039) as independent predictors of NIBL. CONCLUSIONS: HR-MRI-derived vulnerable plaque markers (PE and PR) are closely associated with the occurrence of NIBL following EVT for BAS, providing imaging-based evidence for risk stratification and treatment optimization.

articles.title: The clinical application of a low-profile stent for symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis in the middle cerebral artery: a retrospective study of the Atlas stent.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS) is a major cause of ischemic stroke, conferring high recurrence risk especially among East Asian populations. Landmark trials revealed limitations of Wingspan stenting, including restenosis concerns. The low-profile, flexible Neuroform Atlas stent, initially designed for intracranial aneurysms, may be suitable for tortuous intracranial vessels, yet its real-world evidence for middle cerebral artery (MCA)-segment symptomatic ICAS (sICAS) remains insufficient. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the Neuroform Atlas stent for treating sICAS involving the MCA M1-M2 segment and explore the clinical value of individualized balloon dilation strategies. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 22 consecutive patients with severe sICAS (70-99% stenosis) in the MCA M1-M2 segment, who were treated with the Neuroform Atlas stent at our center between November 2021 and June 2025. The primary endpoints were technical success rate, perioperative complications, and improvement in vascular stenosis immediately after the procedure and at the 6-month follow-up, including the incidence of in-stent restenosis. An exploratory analysis was performed on cases with different balloon dilation strategies. RESULTS: The technical success rate was 100% in all 22 cases, with no perioperative stroke or death. The mean preprocedural stenosis rate was 80.86%±9.82%, which decreased immediately after the procedure to 32.34%±10.36% (P<0.01). Among the 19 patients who completed imaging follow-up, the mean residual stenosis rate at 6 months was 38.43%±21.39%, showing no statistically significant difference compared with the immediate postprocedural value (P>0.05). The restenosis rate was 10.53% (2/19), with both cases being asymptomatic and occurring in Mori type B or C lesions. The multiple balloon dilation group had a higher baseline stenosis degree, but no statistically significant difference was observed between the two groups in either the immediate postprocedural residual stenosis rate or the 6-month residual stenosis rate. CONCLUSIONS: The Neuroform Atlas stent is safe and effective for treating sICAS in the MCA M1-M2 segment. An individualized balloon predilation strategy can optimize immediate lumen reconstruction for complex lesions without significantly affecting long-term patency. The inherent complexity of the lesion itself may be associated with postoperative restenosis.

articles.title: Serial changes in right ventricular function after mitral valve surgery: retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the clinical relevance of right ventricular (RV) function assessed on echocardiography, its predictive utility for patients receiving mitral valve surgery remains uncertain. The primary objectives of this study were to characterize RV function before and after valvular surgery and to establish the diagnostic value of this assessment. METHODS: Echocardiograms were collected prospectively from patients undergoing mitral valve surgery between 2020 and 2023. Subsequently, a retrospective analysis of preoperative and postoperative echocardiographic parameters was performed to evaluate RV function, including tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S'TDI), RV fractional area change (FAC), RV free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS), RV global longitudinal strain (RVGLS), and three-dimensional RV ejection fraction (3D RVEF). The study included 115 patients with mitral valve surgery. Serial echocardiographic evaluations were performed at four time points: preoperatively, 1 week postoperatively, 6 months postoperatively, and 1 year postoperatively. Serial changes in echocardiographic parameters (TAPSE, FAC, S'TDI, RVFWLS, and 3D‑RVEF) were analyzed via repeated‑measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and DeLong tests were used to evaluate and compare diagnostic performance. Reproducibility for RVFWLS, RVGLS, and 3D‑RVEF was assessed according to intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman plots in a random subset of 20 observations. RESULTS: The principal findings were as follows: (I) RV systolic function demonstrated a statistically significant reduction postoperatively as compared to the preoperative baseline level (P<0.0001). (II) One year after operation, TAPSE and S'TDI remained significantly lower than their corresponding preoperative values, with mean changes of -0.34 mm [95% confidence interval (CI): -0.55 to -0.14; P=0.0003] and 1.48 cm/s (95% CI: 0.45 to 2.52; P=0.0024), respectively. In contrast, RVFWLS and 3D RVEF recovered to levels comparable to those at baseline, with mean changes of 0.29% (95% CI: -2.19% to 2.77%; P>0.05) and -3.04% (95% CI: -9.98% to 3.91%; P>0.05), respectively. (III) According to the DeLong test, RVFWLS demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for RV systolic dysfunction (area under the curve =0.771), significantly outperforming conventional parameters (FAC, TAPSE, and S'TDI; all P values <0.001). (IV) RVFWLS exhibited stronger diagnostic agreement with the reference standard (3D RVEF) in identifying impaired RV systolic function, as indicated by the reclassification rate (31%), as compared to conventional parameters (57-64%). CONCLUSIONS: RVFWLS may serve as a novel indicator for assessing RV systolic function both preoperatively and postoperatively in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR).

articles.title: A mathematical framework for pre-mass detection of renal tissue anomalies from computed tomography scans: exploration of a biomechanical signature based on enhancement kinetics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early detection of renal cancer remains challenging, as current imaging techniques predominantly identify tumors only after a visible mass has formed. Lesions smaller than 1 cm are particularly difficult to detect reliably using routine computed tomography (CT). This study presents a novel mathematical framework for detecting early renal tissue anomalies before visible mass formation, grounded in the hypothesis that tumorigenesis induces subtle biomechanical alterations in tissue enhancement patterns that are observable on CT imaging. METHODS: We introduced the Local Biomechanical Index (LBI), a voxel-wise metric quantifying local deviations in Hounsfield unit values relative to an intra-patient renal reference, and a volumetric enrichment ratio (Rt/g) measuring the spatial concentration of extreme LBI values. The single-phase framework was evaluated on a random sample of 20 cases from the KiTS19 dataset using fixed parameters: a 3-mm local radius, the 99th percentile threshold, a 10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm three-dimensional (3D) window, and an enrichment threshold of 2.0. Voxel-level recall, precision, F1-score, and Rt/g were calculated against the reference tumor masks and summarized using means, standard deviations (SDs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Across the 20 cases, the mean recall was 0.575 (SD, 0.231; 95% CI: 0.474-0.676), the mean precision was 0.449 (SD, 0.292; 95% CI: 0.321-0.577), and the mean F1-score was 0.431 (SD, 0.221; 95% CI: 0.334-0.528). The mean Rt/g was 5.223 (SD, 5.427; 95% CI: 2.842-7.604). Recall exceeded 0.50 in 11 of 20 cases (55%), while Rt/g exceeded 2.0 in 14 cases (70%), indicating that candidate anomalies were frequently concentrated within tumor-associated regions. Because KiTS19 provides tumor annotations but does not annotate all other renal abnormalities, the reported precision represents agreement with the reference tumor masks rather than definitive precision for detecting all renal anomalies. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide preliminary evidence that early tumor-related biomechanical alterations may be detectable through spatial analysis of enhancement deviations in CT images. The proposed framework operates without tumor segmentation, relies on interpretable statistical measures, and can be fully automated. Although further validation on large longitudinal datasets is required, this approach opens a promising research direction for segmentation-free early detection of renal cancer and for integrating biomechanical signatures into radiological screening workflows.

articles.title: Echocardiographic characteristics and clinical features of cardiac involvement in Behçet's disease: a retrospective single-center case series.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac involvement in Behçet's disease (BD) is uncommon but potentially life-threatening and may mimic other cardiovascular disorders, complicating early diagnosis. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and echocardiographic features, treatment, pathological findings, and clinical outcomes of patients with cardiac BD, with particular emphasis on the utility of echocardiography in raising diagnostic suspicion. METHODS: We retrospectively screened 186 patients with diagnosed or suspected BD at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University between October 2020 and January 2026. Of the 112 patients who underwent transthoracic echocardiography, 23 met the International Criteria for BD and were determined by multidisciplinary evaluation to have cardiac lesions attributable to BD after exclusion of alternative etiologies. Clinical, laboratory, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, pathological, treatment, and follow-up data were descriptively analyzed. RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly male (82.6%), with a mean age of 43.5±13.1 years. The most frequent systemic manifestations were oral ulcers (95.7%), cutaneous lesions (73.9%), and genital ulcers (60.9%). Elevated inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (87.0%) and C-reactive protein (82.6%), were frequently observed. B-type natriuretic peptide levels were elevated in 91.3% of patients. Among the 19 patients without a history of cardiac surgery, severe aortic regurgitation was the predominant echocardiographic finding (94.7%) and was most often associated with aortic valve prolapse (78.9%). Other echocardiographic findings included aortic cusp aneurysm with perforation (15.8%), echo-free spaces around the aortic root (21.1%), aortic root and/or ascending aortic dilatation (63.2%), pulmonary artery dilatation (52.6%), left-sided chamber enlargement (84.2%), four-chamber enlargement (10.5%), and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (21.1%). Among the four patients with a history of cardiac or great-vessel surgery, all three who had undergone aortic valve replacement developed prosthetic valve dehiscence with severe paravalvular leakage within 2-6 months of surgery. Pathological examination of 14 surgical specimens revealed inflammatory-destructive changes involving the aortic wall and valve, characterized by fibrosis, hyalinization, myxoid degeneration, and chronic inflammatory cell infiltration. All patients received glucocorticoid-based immunosuppressive therapy, and 17 also underwent surgical treatment. At the last follow-up, 16 of 23 patients were alive and clinically stable, four were lost to follow-up, and three had died. CONCLUSIONS: In this case series, cardiac BD was mainly characterized by destructive valvulo-aortic lesions, particularly severe aortic regurgitation associated with cusp prolapse and periannular or aortic root abnormalities. Echocardiography plays an important role in defining lesion morphology and severity, detecting postoperative prosthetic valve complications, and identifying structural abnormalities that may raise suspicion for cardiac BD in the appropriate clinical context.

articles.title: Identification and scoring of factors for ischemic stroke related to cervical arterial dissection: a high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical arterial dissection (CAD) is the primary cause of ischemic stroke among young and middle-aged individuals. This study aimed to identify the high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (HR-MRI) features associated with ischemic stroke in patients with CAD, thereby providing a foundation for future multi-center validation studies. METHODS: This study retrospectively enrolled patients diagnosed with CAD who underwent HR-MRI. CAD was classified into two types: type I lesions, which exhibit only intramural hematoma, and type II lesions, characterized by the presence of an intimal flap and/or double lumen, which may be accompanied by other dissection imaging manifestations. To account for within-patient correlation from multiple lesions, generalized estimating equations (GEE) with an exchangeable working correlation structure were used to compare clinical and imaging characteristics between stroke and non-stroke groups, and between type I and type II lesions. Univariable and multivariable GEE analyses identified factors independently associated with stroke. Using these identified factors, we developed a straightforward score. The discriminative performance of the total score was evaluated through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The incremental value of multi-index assessment compared to a single index was calculated by using net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed with patient-level bootstrap resampling (B=1,000) to obtain optimism-corrected estimates. Finally, stroke incidence was compared across score groups with Bonferroni correction. RESULTS: This analysis included a total of 108 patients, with 125 affected vessels. Type I was more frequently associated with moderate to severe stenosis, and the incidence of intraluminal thrombus and stroke was higher compared to Type II. Multivariate analysis indicated that type I [odds ratio (OR) =3.261, P=0.033], moderate to severe stenosis (OR =3.404, P=0.006), and intraluminal thrombus (OR =3.413, P=0.036) were independent factors for stroke in patients with CAD. The total score integrating these three features showed good discriminative performance for ischemic stroke, with an optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) of 0.747 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.678-0.810], accuracy =0.711, and sensitivity =0.781. Compared with type I alone, combining type I with intraluminal thrombus and moderate-to-severe stenosis significantly improved the assessment of CAD-related stroke [NRI (optimism-corrected) =0.776, 95% CI: 0.533-1.026, P<0.001, IDI (optimism-corrected) =0.107, 95% CI: 0.071-0.142, P<0.001]. Furthermore, as the total score increased, the incidence rate of stroke demonstrated a significant upward trend. CONCLUSIONS: The presence of type I, moderate to severe stenosis, and intraluminal thrombus were closely associated with the occurrence of CAD-related stroke. The exploratory score constructed based on these characteristics still requires further external validation before being used for assessing CAD-related stroke.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of spectral CT quantitative parameters in predicting spread through air spaces of lung adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Spread through air spaces (STAS) is associated with adverse outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Although conventional computed tomography (CT) features have shown predictive value for STAS, the incremental diagnostic value of spectral CT quantitative parameters remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of spectral CT in predicting STAS in solid and part-solid nodules. METHODS: A total of 164 patients with surgically confirmed LUAD presenting as solid and part-solid nodules who underwent dual-phase spectral CT scans were included. Conventional CT features (e.g., consistency, margin, spiculation) and spectral CT parameters [e.g., monochromatic CT values at 100 keV, normalized iodine concentration (NIC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and energy attenuation curve slope (λ)] were extracted. Three multivariate logistic regression models: conventional CT model, spectral CT model, and an integrated model were constructed. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), and AUCs were compared using DeLong test. RESULTS: In the multivariable study, lobulation [odds ratio (OR) =3.509, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.059-11.627], whole tumor size (OR =1.060, 95% CI: 1.013-1.110), and consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR; OR =72.057, 95% CI: 14.619-355.176) were significant conventional CT predictors, whereas arterial λ (OR =0.578, 95% CI: 0.396-0.846) and CT number at venous 100 keV (OR =1.017, 95% CI: 1.009-1.024) were significant spectral CT predictors of STAS positivity. The integrated model achieved the numerically highest AUC (0.842, 95% CI: 0.777-0.894), followed by the conventional CT model (AUC =0.829, 95% CI: 0.763-0.883) and the spectral CT model (AUC =0.829, 95% CI: 0.762-0.883). However, the differences among the three radiological models were not statistically significant (all P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Spectral CT parameters provided diagnostic performance comparable to that of conventional CT features for predicting STAS in solid and part-solid nodules. However, adding spectral CT parameters to conventional CT features did not yield a statistically significant incremental diagnostic value in this cohort.

articles.title: Moran's index habitat and peritumoral radiomics based on digital breast tomosynthesis for predicting Ki-67 status in breast cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The heterogeneity of breast cancer is a key factor influencing treatment decisions and patient prognosis. As a crucial cell proliferation marker, the expression level of the Ki-67 protein is closely associated with tumor aggressiveness, recurrence risk, and prognosis. The goal of this study was to develop and validate an integrated radiomics model based on digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) that incorporates both habitat subregions and peritumoral features to preoperatively predict Ki-67 expression status in breast cancer.
