METHODS: A total of 146 patients with invasive breast cancer who underwent preoperative DBT were retrospectively enrolled in the study and divided into training (n=102) and testing (n=44) cohorts. Intratumoral regions were manually segmented, whereas peritumoral regions (2, 4, and 6 mm) were automatically delineated using mask padding. Moran's index clustering was used to divide the tumors into four habitat subregions. Radiomics features were extracted from the intratumoral regions, habitat subregions, and peritumoral regions. Following feature selection, radiomics models were established using machine learning algorithms. A combined model was subsequently developed by integrating habitat subregions and peritumoral radiomics features with clinical factors. The area under the curve (AUC) was used to assess the performance of radiomics models. RESULTS: In predicting Ki-67 expression status, the rbf_support vector machine (SVM) model, constructed from habitat radiomics features, outperformed the other models, with AUC values of 0.841 and 0.820 in the training and testing cohorts, respectively. The combined model slightly increased the AUC values to 0.849 and 0.852, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: A combined model integrating habitat, peritumoral radiomics features, and clinical factors demonstrated optimal accuracy in predicting Ki-67 expression levels in breast cancer; this model may help clinicians develop personalized treatment plans for breast cancer patients.

articles.title: The initial application of RawVisionTM plaque (RVP) quantitative technique in evaluation for carotid plaque vulnerability.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive assessment for carotid plaque vulnerability is important for risk evaluation of strokes. The RawVisionTM plaque (RVP) quantitative evaluation technique is a novel imaging method based on raw radio frequency (RF) data with real time quantitative assessment of plaques' vulnerability. This study aimed to explore the value of RVP quantitative technique in assessing the vulnerability of carotid plaques. METHODS: In this prospective study, hospitalized patients diagnosed with carotid atherosclerotic plaques were recruited and divided into symptomatic and asymptomatic groups. The B-mode ultrasound and RVP technique color-coded imaging was performed to evaluated the thickest plaque of carotid arteries in all patients. Various quantitative parameters were created by RVP quantitative analysis, including contrast (CNT), homogeneity (ENT), non-correlation (NRT), capacity (CPT) and the maximum value of absolute strain rate (MASR)-were measured as both mean values (from three regions of interest) and global values (from the overall plaque). All ultrasound features were compared between two groups. The Inter-observer and intra-observer reliability were assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). RESULTS: The 123 patients were divided into the asymptomatic group (48/123, 39.0%) and symptomatic group (75/123, 61.0%). Heterogeneous coloring of RVP color-coded imaging in the target plaque could be observed in the symptomatic group. Among all quantitative parameters, the CNT (mean) value of symptomatic carotid plaques was signiﬁcantly higher than that of asymptomatic carotid plaques(65.424 vs. 47.121, P=0.015). And the CNT (global) value of symptomatic carotid plaques was also signiﬁcantly higher than that of asymptomatic carotid plaques(57.720 vs. 37.672, P=0.002). Other RVP quantitative parameters showed no significant differences between two groups. The ICC for intra-observer reliability of the RVP quantitative parameters was 0.791-0.827, and was 0.763-0.794 for the inter-observer reliability respectively. CONCLUSIONS: As a novel non-invasive imaging method, the RVP quantitative technique showed potential value in assessing the vulnerability of carotid plaques.

articles.title: Fully automatic airway segmentation in CT images via dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Precise segmentation of airways from computed tomography (CT) images is critical for pre-procedural planning in navigational bronchoscopy; however, existing methods often suffer from distal branch fractures and morphological losses due to slender diameters, low contrast, and noise. To address these limitations and achieve accurate, topologically complete airway segmentation, this study proposed a novel dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion. METHODS: A two-stage centerline-guided network (TSC-Net) was developed that innovatively combines centerline structural similarity (CSS) loss and centerline overlap rate (COR) loss. CSS loss maintains the continuity of airway tree structures by strengthening centerline morphological constraints, while COR loss enhances global centerline overlap to ensure branch integrity. Additionally, a topology-difference-driven fracture-region completion mechanism was adopted to adaptively repair the fracturedand misclassified areas. The model employs a residual UNet (ResUNet) backbone integrated with an atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module to capture multi-scale contextual features and adopts a two-stage training strategy in which the encoder is frozen during stage 2 while the decoder is fine-tuned using dynamically adjusted loss weights. This strategy enables targeted optimization of discontinuous regions without compromising globally well-predicted areas. RESULTS: Experiments on the Airway Tree Modeling Challenge 2022 (ATM'22), Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI), Extraction of Airways from CT (EXACT'09), and private datasets showed that TSC-Net achieved a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 93.2%±2.1%, significantly outperforming SwinUNETR (92.9%±3.6%, P<0.05), nnUNet (91.2%±1.2%, P<0.05), and UNet (75.6%±4.3%, P<0.05). The tree-length detection (TD) rate reached 95.5%±4.2%, and the branch detection (BD) rate reached 92.6%±3.6%, both of which were significantly higher than those of all baseline methods (P<0.01). Moreover, the segmented distal branches exhibited continuous and smooth morphology. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, our method significantly enhanced both segmentation accuracy and distal branch integrity in automated CT-based airway segmentation through multi-dimensional feature enhancement, topological constraint optimization, and a dynamic completion mechanism. This method holds great promise for pre-procedural planning in robotic-assisted bronchoscopy by enabling accurate visualization of peripheral airways and facilitating navigation to distant pulmonary targets.

articles.title: From localized to long-range: functional connectivity alterations in mild to moderate chronic low back pain patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mild pain can influence brain function, yet its central neurobiological mechanisms in chronic low back pain (CLBP) remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate localized and long-range functional connectivity (FC) alterations in patients with mild to moderate CLBP using static/dynamic regional homogeneity (sReHo/dReHo) and seed-based FC, and to assess their statistical relationships with clinical pain and psychological metrics. METHODS: A total of 55 mild to moderate CLBP patients and 39 healthy controls (HCs) underwent 3.0 T resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) and clinical assessments, including Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), Short-Form of the McGill Pain Questionnaire (SF-MPQ), Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). sReHo and dReHo (sliding window =50 TRs, step size =5 TRs) maps were computed to identify abnormal localized brain regions. Brain regions showing significant group differences were selected as seeds (6-mm spherical regions of interest, ROIs) for whole-brain FC analysis. Statistical comparisons were corrected using Gaussian random field (GRF) theory (voxel-level P<0.005, cluster-level P<0.05). Partial correlation analyses were used to control for age, sex, education, and head motion (Bonferroni-corrected threshold P<0.007). RESULTS: Compared with HCs, patients exhibited significantly reduced sReHo in the third cerebellar vermis (peak t=-4.253, GRF P<0.05), alongside reduced dReHo in the right parahippocampal gyrus (t=-4.796, GRF P<0.05) and left inferior temporal gyrus (t=-3.935, GRF P<0.05). Seed-based FC analysis revealed decreased connectivity between the third cerebellar vermis and right hippocampus (t=-4.678, GRF P<0.05), and increased connectivity between the left inferior temporal gyrus and left pallidus (t=4.441, GRF P<0.05). Patients showed significantly higher SAS anxiety scores (25.15±5.01 vs. 23.08±2.18, P=0.008). Correlation analyses demonstrated that sReHo in the third cerebellar vermis was negatively correlated with SAS scores (r=-0.384, P=0.005), whereas FC between the left inferior temporal gyrus and left pallidus was positively correlated with SF-MPQ sensory (r=0.381, P=0.006), affective (r=0.386, P=0.005), and total scores (r=0.445, P=0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with mild to moderate CLBP exhibit distinct localized and long-range FC alterations within cerebello-hippocampal and cortico-basal ganglia pathways. These neurofunctional changes may contribute to the integration of subjective pain dimensions and comorbid anxiety. Combining static/dynamic ReHo with seed-based FC provides complementary neurobiological insight into how low-intensity chronic pain may affect the central nervous system and highlights the importance of early clinical recognition.

articles.title: Multidimensional institutional learning curve of ultrasound-guided percutaneous transthoracic lung biopsy: a cumulative sum analysis with case-mix assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous transthoracic lung biopsy (US-PTLB) provides real-time sampling of peripheral or subpleural lesions, but institutional adoption requires coordinated improvements in efficiency, targeting precision, and safety. We evaluated these domains using sequential cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from a prospectively maintained institutional registry, supplemented by routine procedural records, for 120 consecutive ultrasound-guided percutaneous transthoracic lung biopsies performed from August 2024 to October 2025. Total procedure time, needle trajectory deviation requiring redirection, and overall complications represented workflow efficiency, targeting precision, and patient-centered safety. Cubic polynomial smoothing identified descriptive candidate transitions, and Chow tests provided supportive within-cohort evidence of structural changes. Adjusted models evaluated associations with case sequence and measured case-mix factors. RESULTS: Candidate transition points occurred at Case 40 for procedure time, Case 64 for trajectory deviation, and Case 75 for complications; all corresponding Chow tests yielded P<0.001. Across three descriptively defined phases, median procedure time was 22.2, 18.2, and 19.4 minutes (P<0.001), trajectory deviation decreased from 22.5% to 14.3% and 2.2% (P=0.017), and complications decreased from 30.0% to 20.0% and 6.7% (P=0.020). Case sequence remained associated with shorter procedure time after adjustment [coefficient, -0.037 minutes per case; 95% confidence interval (CI), -0.051 to -0.024; P<0.001]. CONCLUSIONS: Institutional learning was asynchronous across efficiency, targeting precision, and safety. Procedure time alone did not capture procedural maturity. Reductions in trajectory deviation and complications, with sampling quality preserved, support multidimensional registry-based monitoring. These data-derived transitions are institution-specific and require external validation.

articles.title: Carotid atherosclerotic plaque characterization using dual-energy computed tomography angiography and its correlation with cerebral ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Carotid plaque vulnerability is a key risk factor for cerebral ischemic stroke (CIS). This study aimed to investigate the value of dual-energy computed tomography angiography (CTA) for carotid plaque diagnosis and its associated CIS occurrence. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 103 patients underwent the initial dual-energy CTA for carotid plaque identification and the following brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for CIS detection. The types and components of carotid plaques were qualitatively and quantitatively characterized using spectral parameters including virtual monoenergetic imaging, spectral curve with slope determined as (CT90keV - CT40keV) HU/(90-40) keV, and effective atomic number. These parameters were further correlated with CIS occurrence. RESULTS: Among 232 carotid plaques detected, the number of lipid, lipid-rich necrotic core, mixed lipid-fibrous, fibrous, hemorrhagic, and calcified plaques was 39, 25, 49, 44, 17, and 58, respectively. The corresponding spectral curve slope was 0.31±0.17, 0.27±0.12, 0.25±0.21, -0.99±0.35, -1.78±0.43, and -29.75±2.68 Hounsfield units (HU)/keV, respectively, with statistically significant differences among lipid-containing, fibrous, hemorrhagic, and calcified plaques (P<0.01). The corresponding effective atomic number was 6.85±0.87, 7.01±0.64, 7.18±1.05, 8.15±0.62, 8.31±0.73, and 13.54±1.25, respectively, with statistically significant differences among lipid-containing, fibrous or hemorrhagic, and calcified plaques (P<0.01). The corresponding CIS proportion was 52.63% (10/19), 45.45% (5/11), 33.33% (8/24), 85.71% (6/7), 11.76% (2/17), and 0% (0/25), respectively, indicating that plaque composition was closely related to CIS risk (i.e., the more hemorrhagic and lipid content in plaques, the higher stroke risk). CONCLUSIONS: Dual-energy CTA can be employed to analyze components and types of carotid plaques using multiple spectral parameters (especially the spectral curve slope), thus offering a promising clinical tool for CIS prevention.

articles.title: The impact of hearing loss on tinnitus-related brain reorganization: evidence from multimodal resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether hearing loss fundamentally alters tinnitus-related brain reorganization remains unclear. To address this issue, this study compared features from multimodal resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) between tinnitus patients with hearing loss (TIN + HL) and those without hearing loss (TIN - HL). METHODS: A total of 38 patients with tinnitus (23 TIN + HL and 15 TIN - HL) and 28 healthy controls (HCs) underwent rs-fMRI. Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), regional homogeneity (ReHo), and bilateral auditory cortex (AC)-based functional connectivity (FC) were compared among groups via one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and post hoc t tests. Correlations with clinical characteristics were examined via partial correlation. RESULTS: Compared with the HC group, both tinnitus groups exhibited decreased ALFF in the bilateral anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), along with increased ALFF and decreased ReHo in the left middle occipital gyrus (MOG) [cluster-level family-wise error (FWE)-corrected P<0.05]. Additionally, the TIN + HL group showed decreased ALFF in the bilateral caudate nucleus (CN) and decreased ReHo in the right parahippocampal gyrus (PHG) and middle frontal gyrus (MFG), while the TIN - HL group exhibited decreased ReHo in the right rectus gyrus. Compared with the HC group, both tinnitus groups showed reduced FC between the right AC and the left superior temporal gyrus (STG), with more pronounced reduction in the TIN - HL group (P<0.05, Bonferroni correction). The ALFF in left MOG negatively correlated with the depression scores in the tinnitus groups (r=-0.513; P=0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Hearing loss may differentially shape tinnitus-related brain reorganization. Although both subtypes shared common alterations in limbic and visual association regions, TIN + HL appears to be characterized by disruptions in sensory gating and cognitive control circuits, whereas TIN - HL may involve emotion-regulation network alterations and more pronounced auditory network disconnection. These findings provide a neuroimaging basis for subtype-specific treatment.

articles.title: Ultrasound parameters for predicting high bleeding risk and efficacy of uterine artery embolization in gestational sac-type cesarean scar pregnancy: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is a life-threatening ectopic pregnancy that can cause uterine rupture and severe hemorrhage. Uterine artery embolization (UAE) combined with curettage effectively reduces intraoperative blood loss, but the procedure is invasive and lacks objective preoperative risk stratification. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of UAE and determine whether ultrasound parameters can help identify patients at high risk of bleeding, thereby informing clinical decision-making. METHODS: A total of 161 patients with gestational sac-type CSP treated by either direct ultrasound-guided curettage or curettage after UAE were retrospectively enrolled. Based on the treatment modality, they were divided into a direct ultrasound-guided curettage group (non-UAE group; n=63) or a post-UAE curettage group (UAE group; n=98). Propensity score weighting was applied to estimate the causal effect of UAE on intraoperative blood loss. High-bleeding risk was defined as intraoperative blood loss ≥100 mL. Optimal cutoff values for ultrasound parameters were identified via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and the predictive performance of the combined models was assessed. RESULTS: Propensity score weighting analysis showed that UAE reduced intraoperative blood loss by 41.83 mL as compared with direct ultrasound-guided curettage (P=0.007), and the absolute risk of major bleeding decreased from 29.4% to 3.7% (P<0.001). The area under the curve (AUC) of both maximum gestational sac diameter and gestational sac volume for predicting high-bleeding risk was 0.752, with optimal cutoffs of 2.25 cm and 7.78 cm3, respectively. Adding myometrial thickness and blood flow grade to maximum gestational sac diameter alone increased the AUC from 0.752 to 0.764. The weighted kappa for interobserver agreement of blood flow grading was 0.787 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.717-0.856], indicating good consistency. CONCLUSIONS: UAE was associated with a reduced risk of bleeding during curettage for gestational sac-type CSP. Gestational sac size was the main predictor of bleeding risk; myometrial thickness and blood flow grade showed a tendency toward higher risk but did not reach statistical significance in this cohort. Early detection and timely management are crucial for reducing bleeding risk and improving prognosis.

articles.title: Structural alterations in the superior temporal gyrus associated with depressive symptoms in migraine without aura: a voxel-based morphometry and surface-based morphometry magnetic resonance imaging study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Migraine without aura (MwoA) frequently co-occurs with depressive symptoms, yet the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this comorbidity remain insufficiently characterized. This study integrated voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and surface-based morphometry (SBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) and cortical morphology between patients with MwoA and healthy controls (HC) and to further determine whether structural brain alterations vary across MwoA subgroups stratified by depressive symptom severity, thereby identifying potential structural correlates of depressive symptoms in this population. METHODS: A total of 67 patients with MwoA {38 with lower depressive symptoms [MwoA-LS, 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) <8] and 29 with higher depressive symptoms (MwoA-HS, HAMD-17 ≥8)} and 40 HC were included. High-resolution T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data were processed using CAT12 to derive GMV, cortical thickness (CT), local gyrification index (LGI), sulcal depth (SD), and fractal dimension (FD). Between-group comparisons were conducted using two-sample t-tests within a general linear model framework, with sex, education, total intracranial volume (TIV) (for VBM), mean CT (for SBM), and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA) scores included as covariates. Statistical significance was defined using a voxel-/vertex-level threshold of P<0.001 (uncorrected), followed by cluster-level false discovery rate (FDR) correction at q<0.05. RESULTS: Compared with HC, patients with MwoA exhibited significant reductions in GMV in the left amygdala (cluster size =305; FDR-corrected q=0.046), left parahippocampal gyrus (cluster size =273; q=0.036), left lingual gyrus (two clusters, size =218, q=0.046 and size =177, q=0.046), and right angular gyrus extending into the middle occipital gyrus and precuneus (cluster size =427; q=0.036). No significant between-group differences were observed in any SBM measure. In the subgroup analysis, patients in the MwoA-HS group showed significantly lower LGI in the right superior temporal gyrus than those in the MwoA-LS group (cluster size =73; FDR-corrected q=0.019). Exploratory partial correlation analyses indicated that no imaging metric was significantly associated with HAMD-17 scores or other clinical measures after FDR correction (all q>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Patients withMwoA exhibited widespread GMV reductions across brain regions involved in emotional and pain-related processing. In addition, patients with higher depressive symptom levels showed a distinct cortical morphological feature characterized by lower LGI in the right superior temporal gyrus, which was not detected by VBM. Given the exploratory nature of these findings, the lack of significant brain-clinical correlations after correction for multiple comparisons, and the cross-sectional study design, these results should be validated in larger longitudinal cohorts.

articles.title: Feasibility of vault configuration of the Neuroform Atlas stent in the treatment of bifurcation intracranial aneurysm: clinical observation and hemodynamic simulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coil prolapse and stent-induced vascular deformation during single stent-assisted coiling (SSAC) of bifurcation intracranial aneurysms (BIAs) may compromise branch vessel patency. The vault configuration achieved via the Neuroform Atlas stent (NAS) is a clinically observed deployment pattern that may contribute to aneurysm neck coverage while maintaining branch vessel patency; however, its morphological and hemodynamic characteristics remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to provide a preliminary quantitative description of vault configuration. METHODS: This retrospective study included 35 BIAs treated with single NAS-assisted coiling. Vascular morphological characteristics were evaluated via digital subtraction angiography (DSA) at pretreatment, posttreatment, and follow-up time points. In addition, patient-specific virtual stenting and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed in six cases (with seven protected branch vessels) for quantitative characterization of the branch-protective efficacy conferred by the vault. RESULTS: All branch vessels protected by the vault configuration remained patent during follow-up. No significant differences were observed in vessel diameters or vascular angles across pretreatment, posttreatment, or follow-up imaging (all P values >0.05). Hemodynamic analysis showed that branch-flow responses varied across anatomical configurations. In exploratory simulations, six of seven simulated branches demonstrated smaller flow reductions in the vault models than in the corresponding no-vault models, with a mean branch-flow reduction 5.12% lower than that observed in the no-vault models; however, the magnitude of the differences varied considerably across cases. CONCLUSIONS: The vault configuration of the Neuroform Atlas appears to be a technically feasible deployment pattern in selected cases and was associated with preserved branch-vessel patency in this cohort. Virtual deployment and CFD analyses suggested that vault-associated flow alterations may vary according to local vascular anatomy. However, the observed hemodynamic findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and further validation in larger cohorts is needed.

articles.title: Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging for preoperative evaluation of cerebral microstructure and neurodevelopment in children with congenital heart disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a type of heart structure defect caused by the abnormal development of the heart and major blood vessels during the embryonic stage. With the continuous innovation of surgical treatment techniques and the improvement of perioperative management, the survival rate of children with CHD has significantly improved. However, accompanying central nervous system development problems have become increasingly prominent. This study investigated the clinical utility of neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) in evaluating preoperative cerebral microstructural features and neurodevelopmental status in children with CHD. METHODS: Fifty-five infants with CHD were prospectively enrolled in the CHD group, and 55 age- and sex-comparable typically developing infants were included as the control group. All participants completed the Gesell Development Schedules assessment. The developmental quotient (DQ) and domain-specific subscale scores for five core developmental domains were recorded: adaptive behavior (AB), fine motor (FM), gross motor (GM), language (L), and personal-social behavior (PSB). Diffusion spectrum imaging (DSI) was acquired in all participants, and multiparametric NODDI maps were generated on a postprocessing workstation (Siemens Healthineers). The derived quantitative parameters included extracellular volume fraction (ECVF), neurite density index (NDI), isotropic volume fraction (ISOVF), and the orientation dispersion index (ODI). Intergroup differences in NODDI parameters and Gesell developmental scores were statistically analyzed. Pearson product-moment correlation analysis was then applied to evaluate associations between region-specific NODDI parameters and individual Gesell domain scores within the CHD group. RESULTS: The ECVF in the splenium of the corpus callosum (SCC) of the CHD group was significantly lower than that of the control group (t=-2.261; P=0.026), whereas the ECVF in the frontal white matter (FWM) was significantly higher (t=2.242, P=0.027). ODI measurements in the posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) were significantly lower in the CHD group than in the control group (t=2.401; P=0.018). Intracellular volume fraction (ICVF) values in the PLIC and SCC were also significantly higher in the CHD group (PLIC: t=4.489, P<0.001; SCC: t=2.388, P=0.019). ODI measurements in the occipital white matter (OWM) were significantly lower in the CHD group than in the control group (t=3.707; P<0.001). Compared to the control group, the CHD group had significantly lower ISOVF measurements in the PTR (t=-2.119, P=0.038), FWM (t=-2.825, P=0.006), OWM (t=-2.253; P=0.028), and temporal white matter (t=-2.164; P=0.034). Correlation analysis further showed that Gesell scores, including DQ, AB, FM, GM, L, and PSB, were consistently lower in the CHD group than in the control group. Within the CHD cohort, the NDI value of the PLIC showed a positive correlation with DQ, AB, FM, GM, L, and PSB, whereas the ODI value of the PLIC showed a positive correlation with PSB. The ISOVF value of the genu of the corpus callosum showed a positive correlation with DQ, AB, L, and PSB. The NDI value of the SCC showed a positive correlation with AB and L. CONCLUSIONS: NODDI sensitively detects preoperative cerebral microstructural changes in children with CHD, and its key parameters correlate with preoperative neurodevelopmental performance. Thus, NODDI-derived parameters may serve as candidate imaging biomarkers for evaluating brain microstructure and development before surgery, offering objective imaging-based support for early clinical assessment and timely intervention.

articles.title: Atrial and ventricular mechanical dysfunction and myocardial injury predict long-term outcomes in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction is a hallmark of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and imposes chronic pressure overload on the left atrium, leading to progressive atrial remodeling and functional impairment. Conventional left atrial (LA) volumetric indices reflect comparatively advanced structural alterations and are incapable of identifying early functional deterioration. The present research sought to investigate the prognostic significance of LA and LV myocardial deformation parameters obtained from cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with HCM. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 126 HCM patients and 40 healthy volunteers who underwent comprehensive CMR examinations. LA longitudinal strain (reservoir, conduit, and booster components) was assessed using the fast long-axis method; LV global strain and torsion were derived using feature-tracking analysis. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was quantified to assess myocardial fibrosis. Patients with HCM were followed longitudinally for the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of MACEs. RESULTS: Compared with healthy volunteers, patients with HCM exhibited significantly impaired LA reservoir, conduit, and booster strain, as well as reduced LV global strain parameters (all P<0.05). Following a median observational period of 1,055 days, 41 patients (32.5%) experienced MACEs. Patients with MACEs demonstrated markedly reduced LA strain and LV torsion compared with those without events. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, LA booster strain [hazard ratio (HR): 0.854, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.799-0.914], LV torsion (HR: 0.517, 95% CI: 0.298-0.895), and serum creatine kinase myocardial band (CKMB) (HR: 1.032, 95% CI: 1.018-1.047) emerged as independent predictors of MACEs. LA booster strain yielded the optimal prognostic efficacy for predicting MACEs [area under the curve (AUC): 0.827]. CONCLUSIONS: LA booster strain, LV torsion, and CKMB represent complementary markers reflecting atrial function, ventricular mechanics, and myocardial injury, respectively. Their independent associations with adverse outcomes highlight the multifactorial nature of disease progression in HCM and support a more integrative approach to risk stratification beyond single-domain assessment. Incorporating these parameters into routine CMR and clinical evaluation may facilitate earlier identification of patients at increased risk for MACEs and support individualized surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Evaluation of a personalized total iodine dose (TID) combined with fixed injection duration (FID) protocol using high-concentration (400 mgI/mL) iodinated contrast medium in CT portal venography: a randomized trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The portal vasculature is closely associated with clinical outcomes in liver disease. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) serves as the first-line noninvasive tool for its evaluation. The contrast administration strategy critically influences CT image quality and diagnostic performance. This study aimed to investigate the effect of a personalized total iodine dose (TID) combined with a fixed injection duration (FID) protocol on CT imaging of the portal vein using a high-concentration iodine contrast medium (CM). METHODS: A GE 64-slice spiral CT scanner and a 400 mgI/mL iodine CM were used. The total CM dose was calculated based on the patient's total body weight (TBW) at doses of either 400 or 450 mgI/kg. The FID was set at 18 or 20 s, and the tube voltage was set at 100 or 120 kVp. These three parameters were varied to generate eight distinct injection and scanning protocols. Eligible patients were randomized into eight groups. The CT values of the main portal vein (CTmpv), left superior branch of the portal vein (CTlspv), and liver parenchyma (CTliver), image noise, contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), volume CT dose index (CTDIvol), and dose-length product (DLP) were measured. Additionally, overall image quality, portal vein lesion detection, liver lesion detectability, maximum intensity projection (MIP), and volume rendering (VR) reconstructions of the portal vein were evaluated. RESULTS: Lower tube voltage significantly increased CTmpv (P<0.001, partial η2=0.229), CTlspv (P<0.001, partial η2=0.127), CTliver (P<0.001, partial η2=0.089), and image noise (P<0.001, partial η2=0.118), while significantly reducing CTDIvol (P<0.001, partial η2=0.152) and DLP (P<0.001, partial η2=0.209). FID significantly affected CTmpv (P=0.039, partial η2=0.025) and CNR (P=0.009, partial η2=0.04) (both CTmpv and CNR were higher in the 20 s FID group than in the 18 s group). In the subjective evaluation, tube voltage significantly influenced portal vein lesion detection (P=0.004, partial η2=0.048); other scores (overall image quality, liver lesion detectability, VR, and MIP) showed no significant differences among the three factors, with no interactions. Meanwhile, the main effect of TID and FID, as well as all interaction effects, was non-significant (P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: When using high-concentration iodine CM, all imaging protocols achieved satisfactory portal vein enhancement. The protocol combining a lower flow rate (20-s FID), a lower TID (400 mgI/kg), and a tube voltage of 100 kVp improved portal vein CT values and reduced radiation dose without compromising image quality, and thus represents a promising protocol for clinical CT portal venography.

articles.title: Post-thrombolysis computed tomography angiography and perfusion features associated with an unfavorable early neurological response: a single-center retrospective study in a clinically selected anterior-circulation cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early neurological non-response or worsening after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with poor outcomes, but its post-treatment imaging correlates remain incompletely understood. This study evaluated computed tomography angiography (CTA) and computed tomography perfusion (CTP) features associated with an unfavorable early neurological response (UENR). METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, consecutive patients with AIS who received IVT between 2020 and 2025 and underwent CTA and perfusion within 24 hours because of a lack of improvement or initially severe deficits were included. A UENR was defined as an improvement of no more than 1 point or any increase in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score at 24 hours. Patients with an improvement of at least 4 points or a 24-hour score of 0-1 comprised the favorable response (FR) group. Imaging variables included post-treatment vessel patency, collateral status assessed with the Tan score, and estimated ischemic core and total hypoperfusion volumes. RESULTS: Among 185 patients, 62 (33.5%) had an unfavorable response and 123 (66.5%) had a favorable response. The unfavorable-response group had a higher baseline NIHSS score (median 16 vs. 12; P<0.001) and a higher rate of poor 90-day functional outcome. Post-treatment imaging showed a lower vessel patency rate (24.2% vs. 78.9%; P<0.001), a higher prevalence of poor collateral status (66.1% vs. 17.1%; P<0.001), and a larger estimated ischemic core (median 28.5 vs. 6.1 mL; P<0.001) in the unfavorable-response group. In multivariable logistic regression, persistent occlusion [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 7.85; 95% confidence interval (CI): 3.60-16.80], poor collateral status (aOR, 4.05; 95% CI: 1.85-8.60), and larger ischemic core volume per 10 mL increase (aOR, 1.82; 95% CI: 1.35-2.45) were independently associated with an unfavorable response (all P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this clinically selected cohort, a UENR was associated with persistent vessel occlusion, poor collateral status, and a larger estimated ischemic core on post-treatment imaging. These findings characterize the concurrent vascular and tissue state of patients with early non-response or worsening and should not be interpreted as baseline predictors.

articles.title: A competition-proven deep learning-based dual-domain framework for low-dose CBCT reconstruction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-dose cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging reduces radiation exposure but inevitably increases noise levels, leading to degradation of reconstructed image quality. This study proposes and systematically evaluates a deep learning-based dual-domain framework, named DLDF, for improving CBCT image quality. The effectiveness of DLDF is demonstrated by its first-place ranking in the low-dose task of the ICASSP-2024 3D-CBCT Challenge. METHODS: The proposed DLDF integrates a projection domain model (PDNet), based on a three-dimensional (3D) Res-UNet architecture, with an image domain model (IDNet), based on a two-dimensional (2D) Res-UNet architecture. Low-dose projections were first denoised by PDNet, followed by Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstruction, and then further refined by IDNet. The DLDF was trained on data from 800 patients, validated on 100 patients, and tested on 110 patients. On the validation set, the DLDF was compared with 10 state-of-the-art (SOTA) deep learning methods using five quantitative metrics: mean squared error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), feature similarity (FSIM), structural similarity (SSIM), and visual information fidelity (VIF). Statistical analysis was conducted using the Friedman test, followed by the post-hoc Durbin-Conover test with Holm-Bonferroni correction. On the test set, the DLDF was compared against 8 competing methods submitted by other participants. RESULTS: The proposed DLDF preserved anatomical structures and fine details with notable improvements in overall visual integrity, while also demonstrating improved performance across quantitative metrics. On the validation set, the DLDF achieved average MSE, PSNR, FSIM, SSIM, and VIF values of 0.00162, 35.54 dB, 0.9709, 0.9186, and 0.8492, respectively, outperforming all 10 SOTA methods with statistically significant improvements across all metrics (P<0.05). On the test set, the DLDF achieved an average MSE of 0.00145, ranking first among all competing methods submitted by the participants. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed DLDF effectively improves the quality of low-dose CBCT images. By enabling high-quality reconstructions from lower radiation exposures, this framework may help reduce patient dose and associated health risks in clinical CBCT applications. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Xuzhi-bjtu/ICASSP-2024-3D-CBCT-challenge-Low-dose-CBCT-reconstruction.

articles.title: Medical image encryption algorithm based on Chen's chaotic system and the Advanced Encryption Standard algorithm.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Single Chen's chaotic system or Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) cannot provide sufficient anti-attack performance when separately used for medical image encryption. This study built a hybrid encryption framework combining four-dimensional (4D) Chen hyperchaotic system, Arnold transform, logistic map and AES-256 to fix security flaws of single encryption modules and protect privacy of clinical medical imaging data. METHODS: A three-stage encryption workflow driven by logistic chaotic sequences was designed: (I) the logistic map ran 4,300 iterations (initial X=0.1, μ: 3.57-4.00, step =0.0001). The 100th and 1000th sequence values were Arnold mapping parameters; the 1200th, 1500th, 1800th and 2000th outputs served as four initial states of the 4D Chen hyperchaotic system to guarantee high chaotic parameter sensitivity; (II) Arnold transform realized pixel scrambling, followed by exclusive-OR (XOR) diffusion with Chen hyperchaotic sequences to eliminate intra-image pixel correlation; (III) we extracted 256 continuous bits (positions 2050-2305) from logistic sequences as the unique AES-256 secret key, and implemented multiround block encryption under AES Electronic Codebook (ECB) mode to boost cipher randomness. Simulations were run on MATLAB R2019b with two self-generated medical phantom images: a 743×720 liver lesion phantom (46.1 kB) and a 236×180 splenic trauma phantom (24.6 kB). RESULTS: Quantitative metrics show excellent encryption performance. For liver lesion ciphertext, number of pixels change rate (NPCR) =99.66% and unified average changing intensity (UACI) =34.73%; splenic trauma ciphertext reached NPCR =99.81% and UACI =33.55%, both above the 99.6% and 33.3% security thresholds. Ciphertext χ2 values were 275.5194 (liver lesion phantom) and 243.3932 (splenic trauma phantom), much lower than plaintext values (1.4977×105, 4.4232×106), proving uniform grayscale distribution. Ciphertext information entropy was 7.9953 (liver lesion phantom) and 7.9969 (splenic trauma phantom), nearly the ideal maximum of 8.00. Ciphertext pixel correlation coefficients (horizontal, vertical, diagonal) ranged -0.0042 to 0.0039, close to zero and far smaller than plaintext coefficients (>0.93). Compared with 2025-2026 state-of-the-art chaotic encryption schemes, our method achieved the best NPCR, UACI and correlation results. Extra tests confirmed strong resistance against chosen-plaintext, chosen-ciphertext, noise and occlusion attacks, with stable efficiency for computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound and X-ray multimodal medical images. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed linked chaotic-AES hybrid algorithm unifies Arnold parameters, Chen hyperchaotic initial values and AES keys via logistic mapping, overcoming drawbacks of independent random module design. It achieves near-ideal randomness, ultra-low pixel correlation and strong multi-attack resistance versus standalone Chen chaos or AES. This lightweight, low-overhead scheme provides reliable end-to-end security for clinical medical image transmission and storage in smart healthcare systems.

articles.title: A z-score-based reference system for renal volume using three-dimensional ultrasound: from model to clinical tool.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of renal volume is crucial for diagnosing nephropathies and evaluating living kidney donors. However, related studies have generally relied on linear models or focused on population-level associations, without providing clinically usable reference standards. This study aimed to develop a physiology-informed and clinically applicable reference system for renal volume through use of advanced nonlinear modeling. METHODS: In this cross-sectional observational study, 634 healthy living kidney donor candidates (aged 20-78 years) were prospectively enrolled at a tertiary medical center. Renal volume was measured with standardized three-dimensional ultrasound (3D-US). Associations with age, sex, body surface area (BSA), and laterality were modeled with a generalized additive mixed model (GAMM), which captured nonlinear relationships. Based on model predictions, standardized z-scores were derived, and clinically interpretable reference intervals were established. Nomograms and an online calculator were developed to facilitate real-world application. RESULTS: A total of 1,268 kidneys were analyzed [median age 51 years, interquartile range (IQR), 46-56 years; 67.0% female]. The GAMM explained 90.1% of the variance in renal volume. Renal volume showed a significant nonlinear association with age, peaking at approximately 53.5 years before declining. BSA was the strongest positive determinant. After adjustment, male sex (-7.93 mL) and right kidney laterality (-5.99 mL) were independently associated with lower renal volume. The derived z-score framework showed good calibration, with approximately 95% of observations within the reference range (-1.96 to +1.96). Nomograms and an online calculator enabled individualized estimation and interpretation of renal volume. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a clinically interpretable reference system for renal volume by integrating 3D-US with nonlinear modeling. The z-score-based framework, supported by nomograms and an online calculator, enables individualized assessment, improving the clinical translation of renal volumetry.

articles.title: Computed tomography-guided percutaneous puncture injection of methylene blue mixed with autologous blood for preoperative localization of pulmonary nodules: analysis of 407 cases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-guided preoperative localization using methylene blue mixed with autologous blood is a commonly used technique for pulmonary nodules. However, its safety profile and risk factors for complications remain to be fully elucidated. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and complication risk of this technique and to explore the risk factors associated with the occurrence of complications. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 407 patients who underwent CT-guided percutaneous puncture of methylene blue mixed with autologous blood for localization of pulmonary nodules during thoracoscopic surgery from January 2021 to December 2025 at the Department of Thoracic Surgery, Central Hospital Affiliated to Shandong First Medical University. The patients were categorized into complication group and no complication group according to the presence or absence of complications. Complications were graded by severity according to the Clavien-Dindo classification. The clinical data of patients in the two groups were compared by univariable analysis and multivariable logistic regression analysis to explore the independent risk factors for patients to develop complications during localization, and to establish and validate the nomogram prediction model. RESULTS: The localization success rate was 99.75% (406/407). For the single failed case, the nodule could still be located with the aid of preoperative imaging. The overall complication rate was 8.11% (33/407). The most common complication was pneumothorax, occurring in 7.37% (30/407) of cases, none of which required special intervention. Univariable analysis showed statistically significant differences in forced expiratory volume in 1 second as a percentage of the predicted value (FEV1% prediction), prothrombin time (PT), and nodule location between the two groups (P<0.05). Multivariable logistic regression analysis suggested that FEV1% prediction [odds ratio (OR) =0.118, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.054-0.256, P<0.001], PT (OR =0.647, 95% CI: 0.421-0.994, P=0.047), and nodule location (OR =2.916, 95% CI: 1.188-7.156, P=0.019) were correlated with localization complications. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for the nomogram prediction model was 0.855. After internal validation, the calibration curve of the model was highly compatible with the ideal curve with good goodness of fit (X2=5.391, P=0.715). CONCLUSIONS: CT-guided percutaneous puncture injection of methylene blue mixed with autologous blood is a safe and effective method for localizing pulmonary nodules. In addition, FEV1% prediction, PT and nodule location were independent risk factors for complications of this procedure.

articles.title: A wavelet-enhanced state space model for multi-disease diagnosis across chest X-ray, CT, and MRI.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Medical image classification faces multiple challenges, including heterogeneous lesion morphology, cross-modal representation discrepancy, and computational efficiency. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) struggle to model long-range semantic correlations due to their fixed receptive fields, while the quadratic complexity of Transformers hinders the practical processing of high-resolution images. This study proposes the Wavelet Transform-Enhanced Mamba (WTEMamba) model, which integrates wavelet transform with the Selective State Space Model (Mamba) to construct an efficient medical image classification framework. METHODS: The model adopts a three-stage lightweight network to balance performance and efficiency, with core innovations including the design of a Feature Interaction Hybrid Module (FIHM): the convolutional branch extracts local textures, the wavelet-enhanced selective state space branch captures global dependencies and strengthens high-frequency edge features, and channel shuffle is integrated to eliminate information redundancy. Additionally, a multi-scale compressed classifier is built to gradually refine high-level semantic features. RESULTS: Experiments on 9 medical datasets showed that WTEMamba significantly outperformed baseline models such as CNNs, Transformers, and Mamba-based models. In terms of overall accuracy (OA) and the area under the curve (AUC), WTEMamba improved OA over the best competing model by 0.3% to 2.6%, and achieved AUC improvements of 0.0001 to 0.0125. For example, on the Brain Stroke CT dataset, WTEMamba achieved an OA of 93.45%, outperforming Medmamba by 1.99% (*P<0.05 via bootstrap test), while requiring only 2.1G floating point operations (FLOPs) and reducing the parameter count by over 50% compared to Medmamba. On the challenging breast cancer magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and Knee X-Ray datasets, WTEMamba exceeded the best competing models by 2.55% and 2.25% in OA, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The experimental results validate the significant advantages of the WTEMamba model in global dependency modeling and high-frequency detail perception. It effectively balances classification accuracy and computational efficiency, providing a robust and practical solution for medical image analysis. Furthermore, the framework's outstanding performance on multi-modal data, combined with its exceptional generalization ability, highlights the positive significance of integrating lightweight diagnostic algorithms into medical image analysis. Our code and datasets are available at https://github.com/yuting77777/WTEMamba.

articles.title: Performance and incremental value of preoperative multimodal imaging and perioperative clinical characteristics in predicting postoperative major adverse events in type A aortic dissection.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative major adverse events (MAEs) can occur after surgical repair of acute Stanford type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), and conventional clinical assessment may not fully capture the prognostic information provided by preoperative multimodal imaging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a staged risk prediction model for postoperative MAEs and to evaluate the incremental value of preoperative multimodal imaging relative to conventional clinical and laboratory assessment in the prediction of MAEs. METHODS: In this retrospective, two-center cohort study, patients with surgically treated ATAAD were screened between April 2016 and April 2026. After application of predefined exclusion criteria, 1,960 patients were included, comprising a development cohort from Center I (n=1,498) and an external validation cohort from Center II (n=462). The development cohort was further randomly divided into a training set (n=1,048) and an internal validation set (n=450). Preoperative multimodal imaging and perioperative clinical data were collected, including computed tomography angiography (CTA), transthoracic/transesophageal echocardiography (TTE/TEE), admission laboratory indices, disease-severity indicators, and surgery-related variables. Candidate predictors were screened via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression. Five progressively expanded models were constructed to assess the incremental value of Penn classification, echocardiography, CTA, and intraoperative variables. Model performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). RESULTS: In the development cohort, postoperative MAEs occurred in 375 patients and did not occur in 1,123 patients. LASSO-based multivariable analysis identified age, lactate level, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), Penn classification, severe true lumen compression, mesenteric artery involvement, and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time as the core predictors for incorporation into the final nomogram. Model discrimination improved progressively with staged expansion. In the training set, the areas under the curve of models 1-5 were 0.725, 0.768, 0.782, 0.852, and 0.868, respectively; in the internal validation set, they were 0.718, 0.755, 0.776, 0.841, and 0.858; and in the external validation cohort, they were 0.705, 0.742, 0.765, 0.832, and 0.848, respectively. The largest incremental gain was observed after addition of multimodal CTA variables. The final nomogram showed good calibration and favorable clinical utility in both the training and external validation cohorts. Risk stratification in the development cohort demonstrated a marked stepwise increase in observed MAE incidence from 3.7% in the low-risk group to 27.9% in the intermediate-risk group and 74.2% in the high-risk group (P for trend <0.001). CONCLUSIONS: A staged prediction model integrating preoperative multimodal imaging and perioperative clinical characteristics provided effective risk stratification for postoperative MAEs among patients with ATAAD. Preoperative CTA contributed the greatest incremental improvement beyond baseline clinical assessment, and the final nomogram demonstrated good discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. This multimodal framework may support more precise perioperative risk assessment and individualized management for patients with surgically treated ATAAD.

articles.title: Differentiating pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma from solid pseudopapillary neoplasm using contrast-enhanced computed tomography.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm (SPN) and pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma (PACC) represent two uncommon pancreatic tumors with distinct biological behaviors and management strategies. Both entities can present with overlapping appearances on contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT), posing a diagnostic challenge preoperatively. Therefore, reliable imaging differentiation between these tumors is clinically important. This study aimed to evaluate computed tomography (CT) imaging features for differentiating SPN from PACC and to develop a combined model to improve preoperative diagnostic performance. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 68 patients (51 SPN, 17 PACC) who underwent preoperative CECT. Clinical and CT imaging features were compared between groups. Variables that were significant in univariate analysis were entered into a forward stepwise multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and differences between ROC curves were compared using the DeLong test. RESULTS: Patients with PACC were significantly older and more likely to be male than those with SPN (both P<0.001). The tumor-to-pancreas enhancement ratio in the pancreatic parenchymal phase (PPP) was significantly higher in PACC (P=0.004). The "floating cloud" sign was observed more frequently in SPN (P=0.010), whereas pancreatic duct dilation occurred more frequently in PACC (P=0.004). Multivariate analysis identified the tumor-to-pancreas enhancement ratio in the PPP [odds ratio (OR) =1.10; P=0.002] and pancreatic duct dilation (OR =4.65; P=0.036) as independent predictors of PACC, whereas the "floating cloud" sign was independently associated with SPN (OR =0.12;P=0.010). The combined model achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) among all evaluated diagnostic models in this cohort (AUC =0.865). CONCLUSIONS: A combined assessment incorporating the tumor-to-pancreas enhancement ratio in the PPP, the "floating cloud" sign, and pancreatic duct dilation may improve preoperative differentiation between PACC and SPN.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided needle knife release of the transverse carpal ligament for carpal tunnel syndrome: a prospective case series study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is the most common entrapment neuropathy of the upper limb and seriously affects patients' quality of life. Ultrasound-guided percutaneous release has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to conventional surgery. This prospective case series aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided needle knife release of the transverse carpal ligament in patients with CTS. METHODS: Eighteen patients diagnosed with CTS were enrolled and treated with ultrasound-guided needle knife release of the transverse carpal ligament. Clinical and electrophysiological assessments were performed at baseline and 3 days post-treatment, including sensory nerve conduction velocity (SNCV), distal motor latency (DML), compound muscle action potential (CMAP) amplitude, ultrasound imaging parameters, and Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) scores for pain and numbness. Telephone follow-ups were conducted at 1 and 3 months to evaluate NRS, Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ), and Short-Form 36 (SF-36) scores. RESULTS: At 3 days post-treatment, significant improvements were observed in the median nerve flattening ratio and NRS scores for both pain and numbness (P<0.05). At 1 and 3 months, significant improvements were maintained in pain intensity, numbness intensity, symptom severity, and functional status as measured by BCTQ. The SF-36 domains of physical functioning (PF), bodily pain (BP), general health (GH), vitality (VT), role emotional (RE), and mental health (MH) all showed significant improvements at both time points, while social functioning (SF) showed significant improvement at 3 months (P<0.05). No adverse events were observed during the study period. CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary prospective case series, ultrasound-guided needle knife release of the transverse carpal ligament was associated with significant improvements in symptoms, hand function, and quality of life in patients with CTS, with a favorable safety profile. These findings support its potential as a minimally invasive treatment option for CTS.

articles.title: Multi-b-value diffusion-weighted imaging-based habitat imaging for preoperative prediction of histological grade and prognosis in soft tissue sarcoma: focusing on intratumoral heterogeneity.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Marked intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) is a critical biological characteristic of soft tissue sarcoma (STS). This study aimed to develop a novel multi-b-value diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)-based habitat imaging approach to quantify and visualize ITH for the preoperative prediction of the histological grade and prognosis of STS. METHODS: A total of 101 patients were prospectively enrolled in this study and underwent multi-b-value DWI examinations. The true diffusion coefficient (D), perfusion fraction (f), and mean kurtosis coefficient (MK) parameter maps were clustered using the K-means algorithm. The elbow method and silhouette coefficient were employed to determine the appropriate number of habitats. A modified histological grading system incorporating Ki‑67 expression was adopted to stratify the patients into low‑ and high‑grade groups. Differences in clinical features, conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features, and habitat features between the two groups were compared using the Chi‑squared test, independent‑samples t‑test, or Mann-Whitney U test, as appropriate. Predictive models were developed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and model calibration was assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-ﬁt test. Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to identify risk factors for overall survival (OS) and metastasis‑free survival (MFS). RESULTS: Four habitats were identified. Several features derived from Habitats 1 and 3 differed significantly between the low- and high-grade groups (P<0.05). Based on the grading predictors identified by logistic regression, both the combined model [area under the curve (AUC) =0.896, accuracy =87.28%, sensitivity =79.70%, specificity =80.95%, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.837-0.916] and habitat model (AUC =0.841, accuracy =76.75%, sensitivity =69.50%, specificity =85.71%, 95% CI: 0.765-0.916) achieved significantly higher AUCs and greater diagnostic accuracy than the conventional MRI model (AUC =0.771, accuracy =70.52%, sensitivity =62.50%, specificity =88.09%, 95% CI: 0.680-0.861). Survival analyses revealed that high T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) heterogeneity, a multilobulated or other tumor shape, pVol_Habitat 3 ≥26.25% and MK_Mean_Habitat 3 ≥0.913 were significantly associated with poor outcomes (all P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Multi-b-value DWI-based habitat imaging effectively characterizes ITH in STS and demonstrates significant clinical potential for the noninvasive preoperative prediction of histological grade and prognosis.

articles.title: TiLCA-Net: nuclei segmentation and classification in pathological images via task-specialized attention and efficient decoding.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nuclei segmentation and classification in whole-slide images (WSIs) are critical for tumor diagnosis and treatment. Existing methods often face multi-task feature conflict and computational redundancy. This study aimed to develop an efficient multi-task framework that balances segmentation accuracy and inference efficiency. METHODS: To seek an improved balance between segmentation accuracy and efficiency, this study proposes TiLCA-Net, a network that integrates multi-scale attention mechanisms with a lightweight decoding strategy to optimize comprehensive model performance. First, a Task-Specialized Attention Integrated Encoder (TSEncoder) is designed to decouple features by assigning spatial, global, and channel attention at multiple levels, thereby mitigating negative transfer. Second, we introduce an iterative cross-enhancement (ICE) module, which utilizes closed-loop iteration and median pooling to enhance global geometric consistency and robustness. Finally, a Lightweight Context Aggregation Decoder (LCA-Decoder) is introduced, replacing redundant structures with multi-scale aggregation to substantially reduce computational cost while preserving high-frequency details. RESULTS: Experiments on CoNSeP, MoNuSeg, and CervCell-Seg demonstrate that TiLCA-Net achieves a favorable balance between segmentation performance and computational efficiency. TiLCA-Net achieved mean panoptic quality (PQ) scores of 0.528, 0.578, and 0.592 on CoNSeP, MoNuSeg, and CervCell-Seg, respectively, compared with 0.504, 0.563, and 0.578 for HoVer-Net. These results indicate PQ improvements of 0.024, 0.015, and 0.014 on the three datasets, respectively. Patch-level benchmarking showed that TiLCA-Net required fewer floating point operations per second (FLOPs) and achieved higher batch throughput than HoVer-Net, but with higher single-patch latency and peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory. CONCLUSIONS: Through feature decoupling and efficient decoder reconstruction, TiLCA-Net provides a practical accuracy-efficiency trade-off for patch-level nuclei analysis in computational pathology.

articles.title: Prognostic value of pulmonary artery pulsatility index for perioperative adverse cardiovascular events in patients undergoing surgery for mitral regurgitation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi) demonstrates prognostic value across cardiopulmonary conditions, yet its utility in mitral regurgitation (MR) perioperative risk stratification remains undefined. This study aimed to evaluate whether the PAPi could independently predict perioperative adverse cardiovascular events in patients with MR, and to explore whether its addition to the European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II provided incremental value. METHODS: This ambidirectional cohort study enrolled 302 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe MR undergoing mitral valve surgery. PAPi was calculated as pulmonary artery pulse pressure (pulmonary artery systolic pressure minus diastolic pressure) divided by right atrial pressure, all estimated by echocardiography. Patients were grouped by PAPi tertiles and followed for 3 months. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Exploratory endpoints included mechanical ventilation duration and inotropic support. Incremental value was assessed by integrating PAPi into EuroSCORE II. RESULTS: Patients were stratified into low PAPi (<3.4, n=99), intermediate PAPi (3.4-4.8, n=101), and high PAPi (>4.8, n=102) groups. MACE incidence was 37.4% (37/99), 10.9% (11/101), and 3.9% (4/102), respectively (χ2=43.70, P<0.001). Lower PAPi was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, inotropic support, and intensive care unit (ICU) stay (all P<0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis showed that PAPi predicted MACE with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.82 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.76-0.88]. At cutoff 3.45, sensitivity was 81%, specificity 75%, positive predictive value (PPV) 40.0%, and negative predictive value (NPV) 94.9%. Bootstrap validation confirmed stability (AUC 0.82, 95% CI: 0.761-0.878). Multivariate analysis identified PAPi [odds ratio (OR) =0.26, 95% CI: 0.15-0.45, P<0.001], EuroSCORE II (OR=1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.28, P=0.012), and tricuspid annular plane systolicexcursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure [TAPSE/PASP; OR =0.79 per 1-standard deviation (SD) decrease, 95% CI: 0.65-0.95, P=0.013] as independent predictors. Each 1-unit PAPi decrease was associated with a 3.8-fold increase in MACE risk. Adding PAPi to clinical risk score and echocardiographic right ventricular function models improved predictive performance [C-statistic 0.70 to 0.85; net reclassification improvement (NRI) =0.807; integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) =0.144; all P<0.001]. Bootstrap optimism correction yielded an AUC of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.80-0.90). Subgroup analyses showed consistent predictive value (all interaction P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: The echocardiography-derived PAPi predicts perioperative MACE in patients with MR. Incorporation of this index into traditional risk scoring systems provides incremental value for preoperative risk assessment and facilitates the identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Test-bolus peak attenuation for predicting aortic enhancement in coronary computed tomography angiography: an exploratory subgroup analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adequate intravascular enhancement is essential for accurate coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) evaluation; however, conventional empirical contrast protocols often result in significant variability in enhancement because they do not account for individual physiological differences. Test-bolus techniques represent a potential approach for individualized contrast delivery; however, their precise quantitative relationship with final vascular enhancement requires further clarification. This study aimed to investigate the quantitative association between test-bolus peak attenuation and final aortic enhancement (FAE) in CCTA and to describe subgroup variations based on body mass index (BMI) and cardiac output (CO). METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 50 patients who underwent CCTA. Test-bolus peak attenuation and FAE were systematically recorded. To evaluate the quantitative association between test-bolus peak attenuation and FAE, univariate linear regression analysis was performed, followed by subgroup analyses stratified by BMI (normal, overweight, or obese) and CO (normal or high). RESULTS: Test-bolus peak attenuation was a significant positive predictor of FAE (β=0.924, P<0.001), accounting for 26.1% of the overall variance in FAE. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed descriptive differences in the strength of this predictive trend across BMI categories. Notably, a stronger predictive trend was observed in obese patients (R2=0.812, P=0.037) than in normal weight (R2=0.310) and overweight (R2=0.247) patients. Conversely, while predictive efficacy remained significant in patients with normal CO (R2=0.288, P=0.001), it was attenuated and statistically non-significant in those with high CO (R2=0.240, P=0.090). CONCLUSIONS: Test-bolus peak attenuation demonstrated significant potential as a quantitative predictor of aortic enhancement in CCTA, suggesting that test-bolus peak attenuation may be useful in exploring individualized contrast protocols. The descriptive trends observed in the obese subgroup are strictly hypothesis-generating. Exploratory findings suggest that the predictive trend might vary according to BMI and CO. Larger studies are needed to confirm these descriptive observations.

articles.title: Real-time three-dimensional echocardiographic assessment of the association between aortic diameter and left ventricular mechanical dyssynchrony in patients with bicuspid aortic valve.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is frequently accompanied by aortic dilation (AD), which may impair left ventricular (LV) function. However, research on the relationship between aortic diameter and left ventricular mechanical dyssynchrony (LVMD) is limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between the body surface area (BSA)-indexed aortic size index (ASI) and the three-dimensional systolic dyssynchrony index (3D-SDI) as assessed by real-time three-dimensional echocardiography (RT-3DE) in patients with BAV. METHODS: This study retrospectively included 79 patients with BAV and 40 normal individuals. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) was used to measure the internal diameters of the sinus of Valsalva and the ascending aorta in patients with BAV. These measurements were indexed to BSA to calculate the sinus of Valsalva size index (SOVSI) and the ascending aortic size index (AASI), respectively. Patients with BAV were divided into two groups based on the SOVSI and AASI, respectively: the non-dilated group (≤2.1 cm/m²) and the dilated group (>2.1 cm/m²). RT-3DE was used to measure the standard deviation (SD) and maximal difference in the time to minimum systolic volume (Tmsv) across 16, 12, and 6 LV segments. These parameters were expressed as percentages of the cardiac cycle (Tmsv16/12/6-SD% and Tmsv16/12/6-Dif%, respectively). Spearman correlation analysis was conducted to assess the associations between the study variables and Tmsv16-SD%. Multiple linear regression analysis was then performed to identify the factors independently associated with Tmsv16-SD%. RESULTS: Compared with the controls, patients with BAV exhibited LVMD, as indicated by increased Tmsv16-SD%, Tmsv12-SD%, Tmsv6-SD%, Tmsv16-Dif%, Tmsv12-Dif%, and Tmsv6-Dif%. This increase was more pronounced in the dilated group than in the non-dilated group (P<0.001); however, no significant difference in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was observed between these two subgroups. Among patients with BAV, those with dilation of the sinus of Valsalva or the ascending aorta also had lower E/A (E, peak early diastolic mitral inflow velocity; A, peak late diastolic mitral inflow velocity) ratios and higher E/e' (e', peak early diastolic mitral annular velocity) ratios. In a multiple linear regression analysis, Tmsv16-SD% was independently associated with SOVSI (β=4.447, P<0.001), AASI (β=3.388, P<0.001), and E/e' (β=0.727, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with BAV exhibit LVMD, which is more pronounced in those with concomitant AD. Both SOVSI and AASI are independently associated with LVMD. The study findings provide further evidence of an association between AD and greater LVMD in patients with BAV.

articles.title: Predictive value of cardiac magnetic resonance atrial and ventricular strain for adverse prognosis in patients with myocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocarditis refers to an inflammatory response of myocardial tissue caused by various causes. Patients with myocarditis are at high risk of adverse prognosis, defined as major adverse cardiac events (MACEs). Atrial and ventricles strain analysis using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays a crucial role in the prognostic evaluation of myocarditis. This meta-analysis provides the first comprehensive evaluation of the predictive value of atrial and ventricular strain derived from CMR for MACE in patients with myocarditis. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, OVID Medline, Scopus, Sinomed, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP Database, and the search time range spans from the establishment of the database to June 2026. The level of evidence was assessed based on meta-analyses of the hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of atrial and ventricular strain parameters for predicting MACE. Fixed-effect or random-effect models were used to synthesize data, with I2 and sensitivity analyses for heterogeneity. RESULTS: A total of 18 studies involving 3,454 participants were included, comprising 15 studies on left ventricular (LV) strain, 8 on right ventricular (RV) strain, and 8 on left atrial (LA) strain. Regarding LV myocardial strain, global longitudinal strain (GLS) (HR 1.22, 95% CI: 1.13-1.31), global circumferential strain (GCS) (HR 1.18, 95% CI: 1.10-1.28), and global radial strain (GRS) (HR 0.91, 95% CI: 0.86-0.95) all showed prognostic value for MACE in acute myocarditis. The timing of magnetic resonance (MR) examination is critical, and imaging appears to be most informative when performed within 2 weeks, or even within 1 week, after symptom onset. Regarding LA myocardial strain, Ԑs (HR 0.89, 95% CI: 0.83-0.96) and Ԑe (HR 0.92, 95% CI: 0.88-0.96) showed prognostic value for MACE in both acute and chronic myocarditis. In contrast, RV strain parameters showed limited prognostic value for MACE. CONCLUSIONS: LA and LV strain derived from CMR are associated with MACEs in patients with myocarditis. Incorporating myocardial strain into the management of myocarditis may improve risk stratification.

articles.title: Prediction of late-pregnancy pelvic floor dysfunction: a nomogram model based on proton density fat fraction and synthetic magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) is a highly prevalent condition that significantly compromises women's quality of life. To date, the majority of studies and clinical rehabilitation interventions have focused on the assessment and management of pelvic floor muscle (PFM) function in the postpartum period, whereas investigations into the monitoring of pelvic floor function during the third trimester of pregnancy remain relatively understudied. This study aimed to develop a radiology-clinical nomogram integrating proton density fat fraction (PDFF; Iterative Decomposition of water and fat with Echo Asymmetry and Least-squares estimation, IDEAL-IQ sequence), synthetic magnetic resonance imaging (MAGnetic Resonance Image Compilation, MAGiC sequence), and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) for predicting PFD in late pregnancy. METHODS: A total of 114 third-trimester pregnant women were classified into PFD and non-PFD groups. Fat fraction (FF), T1, T2, proton density (PD), and fractional anisotropy (FA) of bilateral levator ani muscles (LAMs) were measured from IDEAL-IQ, MAGiC, and DTI by two radiologists (with 15 years of experience). Measurement reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Univariate analysis screened potential predictors [age, gestational week, gravida, parity, delivery mode, fetal weight, pre- and post-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and quantitative imaging parameters]. Significant variables were included in a multivariate logistic regression to build the nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: Of 114 participants, 52 were assigned to the PFD group and 62 to the non-PFD group. Univariate analysis showed significant between-group differences in gestational week (P=0.025), gravida (P=0.032), parity (P=0.023), fetal weight (P<0.001), left LAM FF (L-LAM FF, P=0.005), and right LAM T2 (R-LAM T2, P=0.004). The final Akaike information criterion (AIC)-selected multivariable prediction model, gravida, L-LAM FF, and R-LAM T2 were retained as nomogram predictors. The nomogram achieved moderate discrimination with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.726 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.632-0.815]. Calibration indicated good model fit, and DCA demonstrated positive net benefit within a threshold probability range of 25-83%. Interobserver agreement was moderate/excellent (ICC 0.49-0.86). FA was only an exploratory imaging biomarker and was not retained in the final combined prediction model. CONCLUSIONS: The nomogram incorporating gravida, L-LAM FF, and R-LAM T2 effectively predicts PFD in late pregnancy.

articles.title: Quantification of plaque and detection of high-risk plaque characteristics based on coronary computed tomography angiography: comparison between superresolution deep learning reconstruction and hybrid iterative reconstruction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In addition to stenosis evaluation, coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) also allows for noninvasive plaque quantification and characterization, which informs risk stratification and management strategies. This study aimed to compare a novel superresolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR) technique with a conventional hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) method in quantifying CCTA-derived plaque and detecting high-risk plaque (HRP) characteristics. METHODS: A total of 255 consecutive patients (mean age 63.7±9.6 years; 184 men and 71 women) who underwent clinically indicated CCTA for assessment of suspected or known coronary artery disease were prospectively enrolled. The HIR algorithm with the FC43 kernel and the SR-DLR algorithm with the cardiac kernel reconstructed the same raw CCTA data. Total plaque, calcified plaque, noncalcified plaque (NCP), and low-attenuation plaque (LAP) volumes were quantified. Moreover, the ability to detect HRP characteristics (LAP, spotty calcification, positive remodeling, and napkin-ring sign) was evaluated. Paired comparisons were made between the two reconstruction pipelines.
